Application of a multiomic-phenomic integrative framework, including iPhenMap (a machine-learning tool), reveals complex molecular programs, including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-driven metabolic reprogramming, and MYC-E2F transcriptional networks governing epigenetic remodeling and perineural invasion. Focusing on RAS-mutant MSS CRC, functional validation in state-of-the-art patient-derived tumoroid and matched xenograft models confirms focal adhesion kinase (FAK), phosphoinositide-dependent kinase (PDK)1/2, and proteasome inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies when combined with mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK) blockade. This work underscores the power of integrated multiomic profiling and functional modeling to refine potential treatment approaches in MSS CRC patient populations.

title: Improved 1H NMR and ATR-FTIR approaches for structural characterization of high-G-block and high-M-block alginic acids isolated from sugar kelp by a two-step gelation method
abstract: Two low-molecular-weight alginic acid fractions, G-block-rich SKP-G1 and M-block-rich SKP-G2, were sequentially isolated from a hot-water extract of sugar kelp (Saccharina latissima) alcohol-insoluble residue by acetic acid-induced and subsequent freeze-thaw-induced gelation. High-field (700 MHz) 2D 1H-1H COSY and TOCSY spectroscopy enabled comprehensive cross-peak assignments for selected alginate diad and triad sequences, supporting interpretation of 1D 1H NMR spectra. Sequence frequencies were combined with previously established inequalities [1] to calculate constrained frequency ranges for homoblocks beyond the triad level. For selected homoblock lengths up to a degree of polymerization of 18, comparison of the experimentally derived frequency ranges with frequencies predicted by chain-growth statistical models ruled out the Bernoulli model for both fractions and the first-order Markov model for SKP-G1. Applying the recently developed logarithmic cosine transformation (LCT) algorithm [2] to first- and second-derivative ATR-FTIR spectra enhanced the visualization of subtle spectral features and produced distinct fingerprints for the two fractions. As a proof of concept, LCT-transformed derivative ATR-FTIR spectra yielded distinct score distributions for the fractions in principal component analysis, suggesting their potential for chemometric differentiation of alginates with different block structures. In conclusion, extending 1H NMR-based sequence analysis to calculate constrained frequency ranges for homoblock polyads beyond the triad level, together with LCT-transformed derivative ATR-FTIR fingerprinting, expands the analytical toolkit for alginate block structure characterization.

title: Metal-Free Oxidized Carbon Nitride/ l -Proline Synergistic Catalysis: Highly Enantioselective Direct Synthesis of C2-Quaternary Indolinones via Dearomative Oxyalkylation Cascades
abstract: Herein, we report a metal-free, cooperative oxidized graphitic carbon nitride/l-proline catalysis for enantioselective dearomative oxyalkylation of 2-arylindoles. The developed method leverages the band structure of g-C3N4 to efficiently generate singlet oxygen (1O2) under visible light and aerobic conditions, driving an oxidative dearomatization cascade. The resulting intermediates are intercepted via an l-proline-mediated Mannich addition, providing direct access to C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones in high yields (up to 88%) and with enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee).

title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.

title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods
abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are indispensable tools for modeling complex phenomena in physics and engineering. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional numerical solvers by directly incorporating physical constraints into neural network loss functions. Despite their advantages, PINN training requires multi-objective optimization, which often leads to significant gradient conflicts among boundary, initial, and residual loss terms. The Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient (ConFIG) method addresses these conflicts; however, integrating ConFIG with adaptive optimizers such as Adam introduces a critical vulnerability: the conflict-free direction generated by ConFIG is further processed by the optimizer, and the resulting weight update may no longer be conflict-free with respect to the task gradients. To address this issue, Cautious ConFIG is proposed as a concise three-line extension to the ConFIG algorithm that empirically restores the conflict-freeness guarantee prior to the weight update. The method is evaluated on three PINN benchmarks: the 1D Viscous Burgers' equation, the 1D Nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and the 2D Kovasznay flow. Experimental results demonstrate consistent performance improvements over the standard ConFIG baseline. Additionally, the stabilizing effect of cautious masking and its reaction to conflict severity, task number, and optimizer lag are investigated using a simple toy system.

title: What the Query Remembers: Query Abstraction Governs Lexical and Dense Retrieval of Classical Arabic Poetry
abstract: How well a poetry archive can be searched depends on what the user still remembers, not only on what the model understands. We show this for Classical Arabic poetry, benchmarking nine dense encoders and BM25 over two corpora, three indexing modes and two evaluation protocols. Which retriever wins is governed by how much of a poem's wording the query still carries. On tip-of-the-tongue queries BM25 leads every dense encoder, including an 8B state-of-the-art model (0.746 vs. 0.717 Recall@5); on abstract queries it falls to eighth out of ten (0.392 vs. 0.748). Editing the wording of the same queries shows that this ranking largely reflects query composition: adding one remembered half-verse raises BM25 by 38 points, rewriting the quoted words by hand leaves BM25 level with the 8B encoder, and BM25's sensitivity to remembered wording is significantly steeper than that of the strongest dense encoder. The same axis controls explanation augmentation, whose effect swings from +37 to -39 points. The mechanism splits by system type: lexical containment predicts BM25's behaviour, while embedding proximity predicts dense encoders. Finally, the field's two standard protocols, known-item retrieval and thematic relevance, dissociate on the same systems, a result reproduced by two blind human annotators and by two open-weights judges, one of them under a rubric with no literal-match criterion. A benchmark that reports one protocol, or one query register, can give a materially wrong picture. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Ellzo/what-the-query-remembers.

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
abstract: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single $s-p$ energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a {\it single} electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.

title: Mechanism-Guided and Data-Driven Design of COF/MOF Photocatalysts Toward H2O2 Production
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a green oxidant and potential energy carrier, and the photosynthesis of H2O2 from water and oxygen offers a sustainable alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process. Due to the tunable skeletons, adjustable pore microenvironments, and designable active sites, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as crystalline porous photocatalysts for H2O2 production.

title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering pH Sensing in 3D-Printed Breast Cancer Models In Vitro
abstract: With the increasing complexity of in vitro models for tissues, cancer, and other diseases, there is a need to develop robust biosensors capable of addressing these dynamic systems. Herein, we demonstrate the use of surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based biosensors to monitor pH in 3D cellular models. We load breast cancer cells with pH-sensitive SERS nanotags comprising polymer-encapsulated gold nanostars functionalized with the pH-sensitive Raman reporter molecule 4-mercaptobenzoic acid, we then seed the labeled cells onto a 3D-printed hydrogel scaffold and expose the model to…

title: Solution-Phase Carbon Dot-Based Room-Temperature Afterglow Materials: Design Strategies and Applications
abstract: Room-temperature afterglow (RTA) materials are promising for bioimaging, chemical sensing, information encryption, and optoelectronic devices because they emit after excitation ceases. Carbon dots (CDs) provide an eco-friendly and versatile platform for solution-phase RTA, but molecular motion and dissolved oxygen in liquids promote non-radiative relaxation and triplet-exciton quenching. This review critically examines the design and performance of CD-based RTA materials in aqueous and non-aqueous media.

title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
abstract: Resonance-induced excessive vibrations can degrade performance, reduce reliability, and shorten the service life of engineering structures. To reduce the risk of resonance, structural natural frequencies are generally engineered to be shifted away from excitation frequencies. To achieve these frequency shifts, topology optimization provides a systematic approach to tailor structural stiffness and mass as an effective inverse design approach. Multi-material topology optimization exploits the high-dimensional design space of spatially varying material constituents by simultaneously optimizing material selection and spatial distribution over the design domain, offering great flexibility in controlling natural frequencies. This study proposes a multi-material topology optimization that attenuates excessive structural dynamic vibrations in free-vibration scenarios via a novel multivariate weight-based interpolation method. Additionally, to address non-smoothness due to mode switching amid optimization, we employ a bound formulation with an auxiliary scalar design variable to replace the max-min eigenvalue objective with constraints on individual eigenvalues. Furthermore, we study and compare three optimization formulations for multi-material design to attenuate vibrations, including maximizing fundamental eigenfrequency, maximizing the gap between adjacent eigenfrequencies, and excluding frequencies from targeted frequency bands, which are smoothly approximated by a proposed rational polynomial formulation. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of our proposed method.

title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
abstract: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation. Specifically, we model wave propagation by Floquet-Bloch theory and solve the resulting eigenvalue problem by the finite element method along the boundary of the irreducible Brillouin zone. We first propose a multivariate weight-based method via a novel interpolation scheme that maps the design variables of an arbitrary number of candidate materials into effective density and stiffness for elastic wave-propagation calculations, where bandgaps arise from the contrast in the stiffness and inertia among material constituents. We then develop two formulations for bandgap optimization. The first formulation maximizes the gap between two adjacent frequency bands using a bound-based approach, where we introduce two auxiliary scalar variables as additional design variables and incorporate them directly into the design objective, yielding a linear, differentiable design objective, with the eigenfrequencies entering the formulation through associated constraints. The second formulation places a bandgap over a user-defined target frequency range through a dynamic band-pairing strategy, where we adaptively identify the relevant pair of adjacent bands amid optimization iterations. Towards the end, we validate the bandgap performance of our designs against the transmission loss spectra computed from COMSOL Multiphysics.

title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. Structural analysis of the latter sample revealed a high density of strain-relieving interfacial dislocations, identified primarily as Lomer-type or 60°-type, that accommodated the ~4% lattice mismatch between the two materials, while chemical analysis showed very limited interfacial intermixing. Crystallographic analysis showed that the interface faceting was associated with rutile {101} facets, with characteristic facet angles of ~114°; these observations support thermally driven TiO2 (001) substrate faceting rather than an interface reconstruction resulting from GeO2 epitaxy. Overall, these findings provide useful insights into the mechanisms governing interface formation and strain relaxation in r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructures and suggest that further refinement of growth conditions should enable improved epitaxial growth of r-GeO2 for future ultrawide-bandgap electronic device applications.

title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

title: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) under finite electric displacement fields: a removable $α\!\to\!δ$ reorientation barrier and a persistent first-order $δ\!\to\!β$ conformational change
abstract: The $α$, $δ$, and $β$ phases of PVDF are interconverted by electrical poling and mechanical drawing, yet the thermodynamics under a controlled electrical boundary condition has not been established from first principles. We evaluate the zero-temperature free energy at fixed electric displacement $D$ from van der Waals density-functional calculations along two constrained coordinates in a common 24-atom cell: a tilt of the gauche C--C bonds that maps antipolar $α$ onto polar $δ$ (cell change $<1\%$), and a backbone torsion that straightens TG$^+$TG$^-$ chains into all-trans $β$ (chain-repeat strain $10.6\%$). As $D$ increases from 0 to $0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, the lowest homogeneous free energy switches from $α$ to $δ$ at $D_{c1}=0.046$~C\,m$^{-2}$ and from $δ$ to $β$ at $D_{c2}=0.157$~C\,m$^{-2}$. At $T=0$ with domain-wall energy neglected, a $δ$ multidomain state lies $14.3$~meV per cell below homogeneous $α$ at every $D$. A $Γ$-point harmonic estimate suggests that vibrations reverse this ordering at room temperature. $δ$ and $β$ coexist for $0.11<D<0.21$~C\,m$^{-2}$ at $E^*=0.69$~GV\,m$^{-1}$, independent of the screening constant. The tilt barrier falls from $0.66$~eV per cell at $D=0$ to $17$~meV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$ (below $k_BT$ at $300$~K), while the torsion barrier remains $0.66$~eV at $D_{c2}$ and $0.34$~eV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, so $δ\toβ$ stays first order. Much of the difference traces to the path effective charge ($0.28e$ for the tilt, $0.18e$ for the torsion). Scaling shows the tilt barrier would survive with the torsion charge; the smaller torsion charge accounts for about half the barrier it retains. The landscape accounts for why a field produces $δ$ and why $β$ is reached by drawing, and suggests that raising that charge could let a field alone produce $β$.

title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.

title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
abstract: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

title: Complementary Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
abstract: N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: AlphaFold3 Pseudo-Ensembles Capture β-Sheet Organization and Structural Diversity of Short Amyloidogenic Peptides
abstract: Beyond predicting unique native globular protein structures, AlphaFold has been used to sample conformational diversity in globular proteins. Here, we asked whether this capacity can be transferred to amyloid fibrils formed by short peptides, despite the fundamental difficulties posed by their polymorphism, sensitivity to environmental variables such as pH and cofactors, limited evolutionary constraints, and underrepresentation of amyloids in structural databases. Using a comprehensive set of short amyloidogenic peptides, we show that sets of AlphaFold3 (AF3) models (pseudo-ensembles) are accurate predictors of parallel versus antiparallel β-sheet organization, correctly assigning 112 of the 117 peptides for which a clear preference is predicted. Moreover, the simultaneous sampling of both organizations provides a signature of structural diversity, as shown for the polymorphic peptides MVGGVVIA and LYIQWL. Modeling of the precise steric-zipper architecture is less reliable and biased toward compact arrangements, while prediction in the presence of cosolvents and metal ions does not reproduce solvent-mediated interfaces or noncanonical coordination geometries. Thus, although AF3 does not fully capture the physicochemical complexity of amyloid assemblies, its pseudo-ensembles provide a rapid and useful approach for predicting β-sheet organization and identifying amyloidogenic sequences with potential structural diversity.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Probe-Free, Primer-Programmed Amplicon Encoding Enables Nanopore-Based Multiplex Detection With Deep Learning Decoding.
abstract: Single-reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co-amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target-specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer-programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target-associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof-of-concept implementation, one-pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six-dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. Event-level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, and aggregation of classified events yielded sample-level calls with >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, with qualitative calls matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across the 9 PCR-benchmarked samples. These results demonstrate a probe-free multiplexing architecture in which target identity is programmed through primer-defined amplicon design and decoded from the resulting multidimensional nanopore response using a DNN, eliminating the need for target-specific reporter chemistry and opening new opportunities for all-electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing based on unmodified amplification products.

title: ‘Journal of Proteome Research’ announces next editor in chief
abstract: Michael J. MacCoss of the University of Washington School of Medicine will lead the journal starting Jan. 1, 2027

title: A Vast Navigable Protein Sequence Subspace
abstract: Fitness landscapes govern evolution. Our empirical understanding of their structure has primarily been informed by evolutionary history. Here, we combine high-throughput DNA synthesis and machine learning, without training on evolutionary priors, to build a high-resolution map of the genome packaging landscape of the Adeno-associated Virus capsid protein. We assay 232,123 mutants around Adeno-Associated Virus 2 (AAV2) including 15 neighborhoods centered on seed sequences within 5-21 mutations of the wild type sequence.

title: Temporal Integration of Weak Acoustic Stress Leads to Delayed Cellular Responses
abstract: Sound is a pervasive physical stimulus with beneficial or adverse effects depending on exposure. While controlled sound-based interventions such as ultrasound have demonstrated clinical utility, epidemiological studies link chronic environmental noise to increased cardiovascular and metabolic risk. Despite these associations, how weak sound is sensed and integrated at the cellular level remains unclear. Here, we investigate cellular responsiveness to acoustic pulse-wave stimulation in human endothelial cells, using intracellular calcium changes as a readout of cellular activation. Cellular responses to acoustic stimulation were compared with over-threshold mechanical stimulation. Over-threshold mechanical stimulation induced immediate responses, whereas single sub-threshold acoustic exposures produced no detectable response. In contrast, sustained sub-threshold acoustic stimulation over minutes produced delayed activation, with onset times dependent on stimulus intensity. These results demonstrate that cells integrate weak physical inputs over time, revealing a delayed activation regime under sustained sub-threshold exposure.

title: From Genomes to Function: Bioinformatics and Multi-Omics Approaches to Insect Chemosensory Receptors
abstract: Insect chemosensory receptors are essential for detecting environmental chemical cues that influence insect survival and behavior. Advances in genome and transcriptome sequencing have expanded the identification of odorant receptors (ORs), gustatory receptors (GRs), and ionotropic receptors (IRs), while also providing new opportunities to investigate their expression, evolution, and function. Nevertheless, the functions of many identified receptors remain unknown.

title: Stimulated geological CO 2 reduction
abstract: Converting captured CO 2 into products typically requires externally supplied electricity or H 2 . Although abiotic carbon reduction has been observed in water–rock systems, productive and verifiable conversion of newly supplied inorganic carbon has not been established. Here we establish stimulated geological CO 2 reduction (Geo-CO 2 R), in which reducing equivalents released during oxidation of Fe(II)-bearing minerals drive productive conversion of supplied inorganic carbon.

title: Accelerated Discovery of Earth-Abundant Oxygen Evolution Catalysts Through Surface-Informed Active Learning.
abstract: The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a challenge in alkaline water electrolysis. Discovering optimal compositions for complex multi-element electrocatalysts is time-intensive and resource-consuming due to the vast compositional space. Here, we propose a hybrid computational strategy that integrates active learning (AL)-assisted screening with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to accelerate the development of multielement alloy electrocatalysts. Our approach employs 15 cycles of active learning, with 20 NiCoFe (NCF) surface configurations evaluated per cycle, totaling 300 DFT calculations. To minimize computational cost, we utilized scaling relationships and calculated only *O and *OH adsorption energies, while the AL featurization incorporated surface configuration information. This methodology filtered the compositional space of NixCoyFe100-x-y alloys and identified the optimal composition of Ni55Co10Fe35. Experimental validation demonstrated that the optimized NCF exhibits accelerated OER kinetics and practical activity, as evidenced by a low Tafel slope of 43.07 mV dec-1 while maintaining 98.68% of its initial performance over 24 h at 10 mA cm-2. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the hybrid AL-DFT strategy for resource-efficient composition screening within the NiCoFe ternary alloy system and highlights its potential for application to other multicomponent catalyst systems following appropriate system-specific model development and validation.

title: Lipid nanoparticle shape and morphology determine the magnitude and duration of mRNA transfection
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNP) are widely used for nucleic acid delivery, with current optimization efforts mainly focusing on refining formulation features, enabling extrahepatic targeting, and improving therapeutic efficacy. Particle shape and internal architecture are variables often overlooked in LNP design, although they critically influence particle stability, biodistribution, cellular uptake, and transfection. Here, we investigate how formulation and process parameters impact LNP shape, morphology, and internal structure, and how these structural features, in turn, influence mRNA loading, cell uptake, and expression. We demonstrate that modulation of lipid composition by increasing DSPC content drives a transition from compact spherical to vesicular non-spherical morphologies, with altered RNA loading at the single-particle level. While non-spherical LNP exhibited higher cellular uptake than spherical LNP, it was identified that this increase was relatively modest compared with the substantially higher and sustained protein expression for non-spherical structures. This suggests that increased uptake alone cannot explain the enhanced transfection performance. The trend was conserved across LNP formulations comprising clinically relevant ionizable lipids SM-102, ALC-0315 and DLin-MC3-DMA. Taken together, these findings establish LNP shape and internal morphology as functionally relevant design variables that should be considered in the design of next-generation LNP with improved mRNA delivery and expression.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals ITGA2 mediates DEHP-induced decidual endothelial dysfunction in recurrent pregnancy loss
abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a ubiquitous environmental endocrine disruptor, has been detected in over 97% of pregnant women. Epidemiological studies have linked DEHP exposure to increased risk of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL); however, the underlying mechanistic pathways remain poorly characterized. This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach combining network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which DEHP exposure induces RPL. Network toxicology analysis identified 143 shared targets between DEHP-associated genes and RPL-related genes, which were significantly enriched in focal adhesion and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. Integration of machine learning analysis on RPL transcriptomic data with MR identified ITGA2 as a genetically supported protective factor causally associated with RPL. scRNA-seq precisely localized ITGA2 expression to decidual endothelial cells, where it was significantly downregulated in RPL patients. In silico gene knockout predicted that ITGA2 deficiency leads to dysregulation of angiogenesis- and immune regulation-associated genes, impairing decidual endothelial cell function and the immunological microenvironment. MD simulation predicted that DEHP forms a direct, stable complex with the extracellular domain of ITGA2. In HUVECs, DEHP dose-dependently reduced ITGA2 mRNA and protein levels and impaired migration. Silencing ITGA2 reproduced this migration defect, indicating that ITGA2 downregulation contributes to DEHP-induced endothelial dysfunction. Collectively, these findings identify ITGA2 as a biologically and genetically supported candidate linking DEHP exposure to impaired decidual endothelial function in RPL and provide a basis for future biomarker and mechanistic studies.

title: Dynamic Interplay of Dissolved Ions and Solid Surfaces Enables Efficient Nonalkaline Biomass Electrooxidation
abstract: Earth-abundant transition-metal electrocatalysts often degrade in acidic or neutral media due to reconstruction and leaching, hindering their use for deep electrooxidation processes like the conversion of biomass-derived 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a key monomer for sustainable plastics. Here, we report that under nonalkaline conditions, cobalt ions (Co2+) and electrodeposited cobalt (oxy)hydroxide surfaces, maintained in a dynamic dissolution/deposition equilibrium, act synergistically to drive efficient HMF oxidation. Carboxylate anions, particularly propionate, stabilize dissolved Co2+ as active complexes that are enriched at the electrode interface, while the heterogeneous surfaces facilitate substrate adsorption. This cooperative mechanism enables deep oxidation to FDCA. By optimizing this equilibrium with a potassium propionate electrolyte, we achieved a 93.3% FDCA yield using only 1 mM Co2+. Coupling this anodic process with the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) allows for low-voltage FDCA production from which FDCA precipitates directly at high concentrations without acidification. This synergy between homogeneous complexes and heterogeneous surfaces offers a new paradigm for stable and efficient electrocatalysis under mild conditions.

title: Magnetic molecular nanorulers enable combinatorial biosensing and determine distances at the molecular level
abstract: Molecular nanorulers are essential tools for mapping intramolecular distances and studying nucleic acid and protein interactions. Here, we present MARs (MAgnetic molecular nanoRulers), a fundamentally new class of nanorulers based on measuring the magnetization dynamics of rationally engineered and ultra-responsive colloidal magnetic nanoparticles with magnetic particle spectrometry (MPS). By tuning the grafting density of DNA receptors on MARs, we reveal surface molecular crowding as a simple, yet programmable parameter to tune the response of MARs over a broad range of target DNA concentrations. We show that MARs can distinguish target binding positions along receptor strands by regulating how much the binding effect is translated into the response. Combining their switchable binding-to-response and DNA hairpins, we show that MARs can resolve the full combinatorial space of four short DNA targets (24-1) in a one-design-for-all fashion, with blind assays achieving 80% best-prediction accuracy. By modelling MPS response of MARs using the Fokker-Planck equation, we demonstrate that their response is well predictable. Using biotinylated DNA constructs and calibrating their lengths for different numbers of base pair, we reveal that MARs can determine the distance between bound monostreptavidin and their surface with a dynamic distance range of up to 13 nm and a resolution of 1.3 {+/-} 0.2 nm. Our study establishes a new class of molecular nanorulers for resolving conformational changes in nucleic acids and measuring distances at the molecular level in free solution via an adaptable, simple, and rapid workflow, making MARs highly promising for high throughput screening assays.

title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
abstract: Altermagnetism, a moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting, has so far been realized primarily in Néel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron-chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g., $\uparrow \uparrow \downarrow \downarrow$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[C_2||{\cal T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and finite inter-chain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the K$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_4$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice $C_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

abstract: The need for minerals in batteries and clean technologies is spurring investment

title: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
abstract: Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Microscale Characterization of Undecalcified Bone Tissue Using Correlative Atomic Force Microscopy and Histology
abstract: Characterizing bone tissue in its mineralized state remains technically challenging. Conventional approaches typically compromise mechanical integrity through decalcification or lack the structural resolution necessary to capture microscale heterogeneity. Here we present an integrated workflow combining atomic force microscopy (AFM) with histological and immunofluorescence assays on adjacent undecalcified bone tissue cryosections. Using a tape-transfer mounting approach, we resolve mechanically and structurally distinct tissue types within a minimally processed single mouse femur section. Furthermore, we show that decalcification substantially alters nanoscale surface topography and local mechanical properties. Applied to an aging cohort of C57BL/6J female mice spanning 7 to 115 weeks, the proposed method detects age-associated changes in bone matrix structure and stiffness. The approach provides a practical methodology for spatially correlating nanomechanical properties with molecular markers in bone and other mineralized tissues, with broad applicability to disease models including cancer metastasis, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis.

title: Differential Protection against Acetaminophen-induced Liver and Kidney Injury by N-Acetylcysteine and Fomepizole in Female Mice
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the leading cause of acute liver failure and is frequently complicated by acute kidney injury (AKI), which worsens clinical outcomes. Although N-acetylcysteine (NAC) effectively attenuates APAP-induced hepatotoxicity by restoring hepatic glutathione (GSH), its efficacy against AKI remains limited, suggesting distinct mechanisms of renal injury.

title: Making the case for a non-primary article
abstract: Author-proposed non-primary articles can bring fresh and timely perspectives to the journal. Here, we discuss the factors that editors consider when assessing proposals for these contributions.

title: Mn-deficient Ni-Mn-Ga alloys: phase transitions, magnetic properties, and disappearance of martensitic transformation
abstract: Composition gradients formed during directional solidification are generally considered undesirable in Ni-Mn-Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys. However, these gradients offer a highly effective platform for systematically investigating composition-property relationships under identical growth and heat-treatment conditions. To exploit this approach, one Mn-deficient and two near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals were grown by optical zone remelting and characterized by X-ray fluorescence mapping, optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, low-field magnetic measurements, and vibrating-sample magnetometry. The ingots contained elongated grains and axial compositional gradients, primarily associated with the redistribution of Mn and Ga, whereas Ni remained relatively uniformly distributed. The martensitic and premartensitic transformation temperatures generally increased with increasing Mn content. Neither transformation was detected between 10 and 400 K in specimens containing 20.5-22.0 at.% Mn, all of which had $e/a < 7.40$. In contrast, both transformations were observed in the investigated specimens containing at least 22.1 at.% ($e/a \geq 7.46$). This abrupt change may indicate a possible electron-concentration threshold for the occurrence of these transformations. Saturation magnetization increased with Mn content up to 25.8 at.%, reaching 96.9 A m$^2$/kg at 10 K and 71.2 A m$^2$/kg at 300 K. Post-growth annealing increased the transition temperatures and changed the low-field magnetic response. The results indicate that composition-gradient oligocrystals serve as an effective platform for investigating the relationships between composition, structure, and magnetic properties in Ni-Mn-Ga alloys with the same processing history.

title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models
abstract: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.

title: Precise Determination of Electric Dipole Polarizabilities of Sr Clock States Using Linear-Response and Equation-of-Motion Relativistic Coupled-Cluster Methods
abstract: We present accurate values of the electric dipole polarizabilities ($α$) of the ground and excited states of Sr using four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) theory within the linear-response (LR) and equation-of-motion (EOM) frameworks. We first investigated accuracy of the ground-state polarizability using the LR-RCC method in both spherical and Cartesian coordinate representations. Upon obtaining consistent results for the ground state, we determine the polarizabilities of the excited states using the EOM-RCC method within the finite-field approach. The uncertainties in our results are assessed by examining the completeness of the basis set, higher-order relativistic corrections, and contributions from higher-level excitation configurations beyond the truncation in our RCC method. We also discuss various procedures for extrapolating contributions to the complete basis set limit and examine their respective limitations. Our calculated ground-state polarizability is found to be inconsistent with the latest atomic calculation, but agrees with other calculations and experimental value. Using the differential $α$ value from the EOM-RCC method, we estimate the fractional black-body-radiation-induced frequency shift of the Sr $^{1}$S$_{0}$$\rightarrow$$^{3}$P$_{0}$ clock transition to be $-5.40\times10^{-15}$.

title: The physical state of the nucleus tracks its function across eukaryotes
abstract: The nucleus is consistently less dense than the surrounding cytoplasm, a difference proposed to arise from selective nuclear import. The functional significance of low nuclear density, however, remains unknown. Because density is a bulk property of the cell, acute perturbations inevitably have pleiotropic consequences. We therefore turned to the natural experiments offered by the tree of life where nuclei vary in genome size, chromatin organisation, import selectivity and transcriptional state, and asked whether low nuclear density is tied to particular nuclear architectures or functions.

title: Macrophage-Derived 25-Hydroxycholesterol Drives Statin-Associated Acute Kidney Injury
abstract: Although acute kidney injury (AKI) has been implicated as a potential adverse effect of statin therapy, experimental evidence supporting this association remains limited. Here, we investigated whether elevated levels of 25-hydroxycholesterol (25-HC), an oxysterol produced by activated macrophages and monocytes, increase susceptibility to statin-induced AKI. We found that atorvastatin and fluvastatin induced cell death in proximal tubular cells when combined with 25-HC. Consistently, administration of low-dose lipopolysaccharide triggered AKI in statin-treated mice. Mechanistically, impaired protein prenylation disrupted the autophagosome-lysosome pathway in proximal tubular cells. AKI was attenuated by mevalonate supplementation, which restored protein prenylation, and by macrophage/monocyte depletion, which reduced the cellular sources of 25-HC. Furthermore, combined exposure to fluvastatin and 25-HC increased kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) expression in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived kidney organoids. Together, these findings suggest that elevated macrophage-derived 25-HC under conditions of infection, inflammation, or major surgery may increase susceptibility to statin-induced AKI. Our study identifies a previously unrecognized interaction between statins and 25-HC and suggests potential strategies to mitigate kidney injury while preserving the therapeutic benefits of statins.

title: AgamOBP4-targeted drug repurposing identifies novel mosquito repellent scaffolds
abstract: Odorant-binding proteins (OBPs) play central roles in insect chemoreception and represent attractive molecular targets for the discovery of novel behavior-modifying compounds. We report two crystal structures of Anopheles gambiae OBP4: one complexed with the fluorescent probe N-phenyl-1-naphthylamine and a second containing two indole molecules simultaneously bound within the ligand-binding cavity. Structural comparison revealed two binding subsites accommodating the aromatic moieties of 1-NPN or two indole molecules, while identifying Thr58 and Thr70 as key residues in ligand recognition.

title: X-ray diffraction from hydrated macromolecular crystals using laser-driven X-ray source
abstract: Laser-driven X-ray sources offer a compact route towards laboratory-scale ultrafast structural dynamics. However, due to the low photon flux available from laboratory scale sources, and the weak diffraction signal from biological specimens, their application to such samples remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate X-ray diffraction from Z-DNA crystals using a laser-driven Cu Ka source (lambda = 1.54 Angstroms).

title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
abstract: Finite element model updating is among the most general approaches to discover constitutive models from structural experiments: since the displacement field is computed rather than measured, it accommodates arbitrary geometries, boundary conditions, and sparse or noisy data. However, every loss evaluation requires a nonlinear finite element solve per load step, and training neural materials requires many such evaluations. Intrusive model order reduction lowers this cost while retaining boundary conditions and variational structure. How can a reduced model remain accurate while the network weights change at every training step? We combine proper orthogonal decomposition and energy-conserving sampling and weighting with adjoint sensitivities of the reduced model, and adapt both the trial space and the sampled elements along the optimization path. The constitutive law is a polyconvex neural network: a logarithmic normalization term, together with a zero-anchored input convex architecture and a growth term, renders the energy polyconvex, coercive, and non-negative by construction, independent of the trained weights. We demonstrate the approach on two experimental datasets and one synthetic three-dimensional example. For a two-phase specimen, training time decreases from nine hours to 41 minutes compared with a full-order identification, without loss of accuracy. In the three-dimensional example, six modes replace 48 672 degrees of freedom, 116 of 15 625 elements suffice to evaluate the internal forces, and training takes 13 minutes. In all cases, the identified material reproduces the measured reaction force and predicts the displacement field from the force alone. Hyperreduction makes the discovery of neural materials from structural data affordable while retaining the advantages of finite element model updating.

title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
abstract: Aluminum nitride-based ferroelectrics combine high remanent polarization, thermal stability, weak size effects, a wide bandgap and back-end process compatibility, making them promising for high density non-volatile memory. However, their high coercive field ($E_\mathrm{c}$) and unclear polarization switching mechanism limit further applications. Theoretical predictions indicate preferential reversed domain growth along the polar axis, whereas experiments show nearly isotropic growth or preferential growth perpendicular to this axis. Here, we combine density functional theory, Deep Potential molecular dynamics and experimental characterization to determine how nitrogen vacancies ($V_\mathrm{N}$) regulate domain growth and $E_\mathrm{c}$. In ideal crystal, strong lattice coupling along the polar axis drives preferential domain growth in this direction. $V_\mathrm{N}$ locally weakens this coupling and promotes polarization nucleation. The spatial distribution of $V_\mathrm{N}$ and the temporal sequence of vacancy induced switching jointly determine the direction and morphology of reversed domain growth. We further show that scandium doping promotes $V_\mathrm{N}$ formation, thereby enhancing defect mediated nucleation and reducing $E_\mathrm{c}$. These findings establish a multiscale mechanism governing thin-film domain-growth kinetics and macroscopic $E_\mathrm{c}$, reconciling experimental observations with ideal crystal simulations and providing defect engineering principles for low-voltage, reliable and scalable ferroelectric devices.

title: Evaluating Artificial Wisdom (AW): A Trajectory-Based Framework for Context-Sensitive Decision Regulation
abstract: Capability benchmarks measure what large language models can do, but not whether their recommendations remain appropriate as decision conditions change. This paper proposes a trajectory-based measurement framework and prospective validation protocol for artificial wisdom, defined behaviorally as context-sensitive regulation of judgment. Versioned reference specifications determine admissible responses and transition materiality before evaluation. Seven stage-level criteria assess judgment under current conditions, while two transition components assess material-update adequacy and commitment-preserving stability. Stability requires prior adequacy; switching within registered commitment classes is permitted, and persistent error earns no stability credit. A nine-component profile is primary, with a secondary bottleneck score and separate critical-failure reporting. Three simplified simulations examine precision, bottleneck estimation, and sensitivity to model-family count. A single-criterion simulation met its precision criteria at 24 scenarios per domain. Near a bottleneck tie, the estimated minimum had a downward bias of 0.55 points at that size. A simplified incremental-prediction simulation detected a Brier improvement of 0.027 with probabilities of .508 and .742 using eight and twelve families, respectively; it does not establish power for the operational protocol. An exploratory predecessor-rubric study comprising 71 evaluation records illustrates aggregation sensitivity but does not validate the proposed instrument. The twelve-family target remains provisional pending feasibility assessment and calibration of the complete analysis. Whether the profile predicts independent decision outcomes beyond capability remains an open empirical question.

title: Global database provides a fuller picture of the elements that make up plant life
abstract: What, exactly, is a plant made of? Scientists have a good understanding of the essential nutrients plants need to grow. But what plants need and what they contain are not necessarily the same.

title: Low-order MLKL oligomers induce irregular membrane defects in necroptosis
abstract: MLKL is a key executioner of necroptosis, a lytic form of regulated cell death associated with inflammatory pathologies. Upon activation by RIPK3-mediated phosphorylation, MLKL oligomerizes and translocates to the plasma membrane to induce permeabilization through yet unknown mechanisms. By imaging single particles of MLKL at the plasma membrane of necroptotic cells, here we show that, upon activation, MLKL transitions from a diffuse cytosolic distribution to discrete, low-mobility assemblies before cell bursting.

title: Calcium-Driven Activation of Gelsolin: Mechanism and the Active-State Ensemble
abstract: Gelsolin is a master regulator of the actin cytoskeleton whose activity is controlled by large Ca2+ dependent conformational transitions of its 6 domains (G1-G6). Despite decades of biochemical and cellular studies, the structural basis of activation of the full-length protein remains poorly understood because active gelsolin is highly dynamic and has largely escaped structural characterization. Here, we combine small-angle X-ray scattering, DEER-EPR spectroscopy, and structure-based molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the transition from the compact inactive state to the actin-binding active form. This integrative approach reveals that activation proceeds through a sequential and domain-dependent mechanism, where different regions of the protein respond to Ca2+ with distinct kinetics and conformational trajectories. Rather than converging toward a single active structure, activated gelsolin populates a heterogeneous ensemble of plastic conformations characterized by asymmetric domain arrangements and extensive structural variability. The two major domain triplets (G1-G3 and G4-G6) display markedly different dynamic behaviors, while actin-binding surfaces are exposed according to a defined hierarchy and remain differentially accessible within the active ensemble, suggesting specialized functional roles for different domains during filament engagement. Together, these findings provide a time- and domain-resolved view of gelsolin activation, establish a structural framework for interpreting its diverse biological functions, and offer new opportunities for targeting gelsolin-associated diseases.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Molecular Imprinting for Efficient Polymer Design and Enhanced Liquid-Phase Separation.
abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) have become significantly more desirable as synthetic polymers with recognition sites designed for target molecules for use in liquid-phase separation due to their high selectivity, stability, and robustness. However, the development of MIPs remains challenging, as the selection of functional monomers, cross-linkers, pore-forming agents, and polymerization conditions often relies on labor-intensive experimental trial-and-error methods.

title: Light-activated catalyst makes sustainable production of hydrogen peroxide more efficient
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) is a versatile chemical feedstock whose industrial production relies predominantly on an energy-intensive process with a substantial environmental footprint. One alternative is to produce it using a catalyst activated by light. In an international research project involving the Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces, researchers have now developed a synthesis strategy that allows them to precisely control the spatial arrangement of ions in a carbon nitride. The resulting photocatalyst is three times as efficient as conventional green production methods.

title: Understanding the Dynamics of Zinc Deposition/Dissolution Processes in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries by In Operando Electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance with Dissipation
abstract: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. Using a three-electrode configuration under a constant overpotential of ± 100 mV, current density, mass change, and dissipation were simultaneously monitored in real time.

title: N-Acetylglucosamine ameliorates knee osteoarthritis by enhancing UDP-GlcNAc conversion and chondrocyte DNA repair capacity
abstract: Background: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degradation and synovial inflammation, while current therapies offer only symptomatic relief. This study aimed to determine whether N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) is superior to glucosamine hydrochloride (GlcN{middle dot}HCl) in slowing the progression of KOA and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms involved.

title: Detection of residues of chlorine-containing pesticides on tomato fruits by machine learning evaluation of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy data
abstract: In this pilot analytical study, we propose the machine learning evaluation of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) data as a new, fast screening methodology for the detection of pesticides on tomato fruits. Five pesticides (acetamiprid, chlorpyrifos, λ-cyhalothrin, tebuconazole, tefluthrin) at three concentration levels down to 0.01 m/v% corresponding to their real application (spraying) concentrations were tested on fully ripe fruits of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum cv. Money maker). Direct (on the fruit peel) and indirect (sampling-based) analytical approaches were both tested.

title: A Dynamic Self-Reporting Metal–Organic Framework System for Catalysis and Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
abstract: Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.

title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
abstract: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer B$_{x}$Al$_{1-x}$N and B$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B$_{0.25}$Ga$_{0.75}$N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V$_2$O$_5$ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6$\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$. A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.

title: Generalized green and red concepts for artificial intelligence, big data, and information and communication technologies: Multidimensional framework and countermeasures
abstract: The rapid expansions of artificial intelligence (AI), big data (BD), and information and communication technologies (ICT) are driving substantial growth in electricity, water, and material demands, with data centers projected to consume 6.7--12\% of U.S. electricity by 2028 (up from 4.4\% in 2023) and AI-related water demand estimated at 4--6 billion m$^3$ annually by 2027. Existing ``green AI'' and ``red AI'' discussions have largely emphasized computational efficiency and carbon emissions, providing limited guidance for lifecycle trade-offs, service-versus-use impacts, and broader sustainability externalities beyond energy. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes generalized green AI (GGAI) and generalized red AI (GRAI) and extends the taxonomy to red BD (RBD) and red ICT (RICT) as well as red electronic and electrical engineering (REEE) \& red digital technologies (RDT) under a unified Environmental-Economic-Social-Technical/Operational (E/Ec/S/T) framework. Based on representative footprint indicators in the large-model era (electricity, carbon, water, and e-waste), we analyze how risks propagate across AI-BD-ICT stacks and across service-use boundaries. We further organize actionable countermeasures into a four-tier taxonomy aligned with the Environmental-Economic-Social-Technical/Operational framework: metric-level reform for accountability, revision of information and communication technologies design principles and demand shaping, efficiency-oriented LLM development practices (data, model, training, and scaling), and energy-infrastructure transition. The proposed framework operationalizes the Environmental-Economic-Social-Technical/Operational-aligned assessment and intervention prioritization across the AI-BD-ICT stacks, enabling sustainability-by-design without sacrificing utility.

title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
abstract: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people. We propose a framework for training teaming agents against Cognitively Constrained Partners: simulated partners whose diversity emerges from procedural constraints grounded in human physiological literature, specifically reaction delays and perceptual limitations, rather than from reward shaping or historical training checkpoints. In a modified Lunar Lander environment, we report preliminary evidence that these partners play more like real people than unconstrained agents do, and that agents trained against them match the strongest cross-play baselines while being the only ones whose performance does not depend on how their training partners were generated. We also describe a human-participant study designed so that its rankings can be compared directly against cross-play, testing how well that standard evaluation predicts real human-agent teaming.

title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $α$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

title: Mapping the Fragment-Binding Landscape of SARS-CoV-2 nsp14 for Antiviral Drug Discovery
abstract: Non-structural protein 14 (nsp14) is a bifunctional coronavirus drug target, combining a 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease domain with an N7-methyltransferase domain. Proof-of-concept data have demonstrated beneficial effects in animal models upon inhibition. Using microscale thermophoresis and X-ray crystallography, we screened full-length nsp14 for fragment hits and developed SAR-by-catalogue analogues with five- to eight-fold improved affinity. Several scaffolds showed pronounced overlap between distinct pockets, complicating structure-based optimisation. Analysis of mutational frequencies across over 14 million SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences identified nsp14 residues with markedly high and very low mutation rates, highlighting sites best suited to pan-coronavirus inhibitor design. Combining these data with all 19 publicly known fragment- and ligand-binding regions on nsp14, most of which have never been directly compared, we introduce a systematic site-naming system and rank every site by its potential for future structure-based development. Weighing criteria include proof-of-principle inhibitor data, cross-coronavirus conservation, mutation frequency, the number of fragments bound per site, and susceptibility to crystallographic artefacts from symmetry mates. This ranked, unified binding-site atlas resolves which of the many previously reported nsp14 sites merit prioritisation, providing a practical resource for future coronavirus antiviral drug development.

title: Dead-Potassium Activation Reconstructing Stabilized Interface Enables Stable Anode-Free Potassium Metal Batteries
abstract: Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. These issues stem from sluggish interfacial kinetics and the continuous fracture of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). A multifunctional electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating bismuth iodide (BiI3) into a carbonate-based system to simultaneously regulate the bulk K+ solvation sheath, reconstruct the interfacial solvation structure, and reactivate dead K.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: When Organic Chemistry Meets Surface Science: From Nanographene Characterization to Single-Molecule Reactions
abstract: The interplay between organic chemistry and surface science allows for atomically precise characterization, synthesis, and manipulation of carbon-based nanostructures. Advances in scanning probe microscopy and on-surface synthesis have unlocked new routes to obtaining fascinating nanographenes, exotic and highly reactive molecules, and controlled single-molecule reactions. Importantly, these developments open access to transformations that are inaccessible to solution-phase chemistry. Here, we illustrate the potential of this approach and outline the future opportunities and challenges.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Dual Reaction Pathways on Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu for Efficient CO2-to-Methanol Conversion
abstract: The design of metal–support interfaces is critical for overcoming the persistent trade-off between CO2 conversion and methanol selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation. Though an inverse catalyst with an oxide-on-metal configuration provides a platform for tuning interfacial properties, the distinct roles of multi-interfaces with different electronic properties and how they collectively govern reaction pathways remain largely unexplored. Herein, we constructed an inverse Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu catalyst to engineer dual pathways for efficient CO2-to-methanol conversion.

title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
abstract: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension $D$ greatly exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy.
