After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using a finite-horizon schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. A recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bounding refitting cost by $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.

title: Unifying Time-Independent and Time-Dependent Franck--Condon Pictures in Quantum Mechanochemistry via the Linear Coupling Approximation
abstract: Quantum chemistry has achieved impressive results in modeling and interpreting mechanochemical transformations at the molecular level. An essential question, the time profile of force application, has however attracted less attention. Here, the Franck--Condon theory of quantum mechanochemistry, previously formulated for the sudden-force limit, is generalized to arbitrary time-dependent force profiles using the linear-coupling approximation. Solving the driven harmonic oscillator yields a closed-form, time-dependent effective Huang--Rhys factor: a natural measure of vibrational excitations upon force application. It is governed by the Fourier transform of the force derivative and recovers the sudden- and fixed-force limits. At the conceptual level, this linear coupling picture links mechanochemistry to vibronic spectroscopy and Marcus electron theory. For a shock-front force ramp, vibrational excitation is shown to be suppressed in frequency, only low-frequency modes being excited under realistic laser-shock-peening conditions.

title: Multireference Polarizable Embedding for Core-Level Spectroscopy in Aqueous Solution: XPS and XAS of Glycine
abstract: Core-level spectra in solution are governed by the interplay of core-hole relaxation, electron correlation, specific solute--solvent interactions, and environmental polarization. We report the first application of RASSCF--RASPT2 combined with the fluctuating-charges polarizable embedding to X-ray photoelectron (XPS) and X-ray absorption (XAS) spectroscopy in aqueous solution. The protocol couples a multireference treatment of core-ionized and core-excited states with molecular-dynamics sampling, and is assessed for the carbon and nitrogen K-edges of glycine in the gas phase and in water. The calculated spectra are compared with experiment and with fixed-charges electrostatic embedding. Gas-phase ionization and absorption features are accurately reproduced. In solution, configurational averaging captures inhomogeneous broadening, while XPS peak positions, relative intensities, and widths depend strongly on the solvent parametrization. The best-performing polarizable model improves the spectral profile, although aqueous ionization energies remain overestimated. For XAS, the carbon K-edge is reproduced close to the experimental energy scale, whereas the nitrogen K-edge line shape is recovered after rigid alignment. These results support multireference polarizable embedding as a promising framework for core-level spectroscopy in solution.

title: Mechanochemical synchronization of force oscillations in connective tissue models
abstract: Cells in a tissue coordinate their behavior collectively by mechanical and chemical feedback with their surroundings. To study how such feedback mechanisms interact, we embed multicellular spheroids from mouse and primary human fibroblasts of different origin in 3D collagen matrices. Immediately after embedding, spheroids apply steadily increasing, radially symmetric, inward-directed forces to the surrounding matrix. Typically, within a few hours, collective force oscillations emerge with an average time interval of {approx}30 min. Similar force oscillations also arise in engineered, parallel-aligned microtissues attached to flexible pillars. Force oscillations propagate between neighboring cells as a mechanical wave, accompanied by calcium waves that travel at comparable speeds of several hundred m/min. Blocking gap junctions or mechanosensitive Piezo1 channels impairs these oscillations, indicating that calcium signaling contributes to their propagation. Their amplitude and frequency are regulated by integrin-mediated feedback in actin-rich protrusions and by ERK signaling, which also controls collective invasion into the surrounding matrix. Neighboring spheroids mechanically synchronize their force oscillations in phase and frequency over distances of up to {approx}2 mm without direct contact. Together, our results show that oscillatory mechanochemical feedback enables multicellular systems to coordinate force generation and invasive migration across cellular and millimeter length scales in 3D matrices.

title: Fabrication of a Bimetallic NiFe-Prussian Blue-MoS2 Nano-heterojunction for NIR-Triggered Antibacterial Activity
abstract: Bacterial infections continue to pose a major threat to human health globally, and the rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant microorganisms has created an urgent need for development of effective non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies for pathogen eradication. In this work, a series of peroxidase-like NiFe-PB@MoS 2 (PB: Prussian Blue) heterostructured nanocomposite (NFPPM) catalysts were successfully synthesised to achieve significantly enhanced antibacterial activity.

title: Examining the Effect of Matrix Composition in Nanocomposite Dielectric Oxides Using Wannier Centers
abstract: Dielectric permittivity is a crucial parameter when designing materials for high energy-density capacitors. Alkaline earth metal oxides are a class of materials with relatively large band gaps and permittivities. Furthermore, introducing metallic nanoparticle inclusions into an oxide matrix provides a reserve of polarizable electrons that in some cases leads to enhancements in permittivity.

title: Terpene Structure Governs Humidity-Enhanced New Particle Formation through an OH-Sensitive Ozonolysis Network
abstract: Relative humidity (RH) impacts new particle formation (NPF) from monoterpene ozonolysis in a non-uniform way. Depending on the precursor, water vapor can either suppress particle formation or increase it, and the chemical origin of that contrast has remained uncertain. Here we use cyclohexane to remove OH and separate the OH-sensitive portion of the particle response from the residual OH-insensitive contribution for α-pinene, β-pinene, and camphene. Experiments were carried out at <0.1% and 60% RH using low monoterpene mixing ratios of 0.5 – 5 ppbv.

title: Microscopic Free-Energy Landscaping and Coarse-Grained 3D Dynamics of Scaffolded DNA Computers: Overcoming Kinetic Traps at Scale
abstract: Thermodynamically favoured molecular computing encodes algorithmic solutions into ground-state equilibrium configurations of self-assembling DNA nanostructures, circumventing the dissipation bounds of non-equilibrium kinetic proofreading. However, practical scaling on biologically derived scaffolds (such as single-stranded M13 bacterio- phage DNA) has been severely constrained by heterogeneous base compositions that create energetic traps, kinetic stalls along long carry runs, and uncharacterized steric effects.

title: Helium Atom Scattering from Cold Salty Water: Impact of Microscopic and Mesoscopic Surface Structure
abstract: Understanding the dynamics of gas–liquid surface scattering is of fundamental importance to interfacial phenomena ranging from atmospheric chemistry to heterogeneous catalysis. In this work, molecular beam scattering experiments and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are carried out to study collisions of He atoms ( E i = 5.8 kJ mol −1 ; θ i = 45°, 60°, and 75°) from the surface of a cold salty water (8 m LiBr (aq) , 230 K) flat jet.

title: An RI-NMR and DFT Study of Boron Homologations: Structures of α-Halo Lithium Carbenoids and the Effect of Boronic Ester Structure on 1,2-Metalate Rearrangement Rates
abstract: Despite the widespread utility of α-halo lithium carbenoids in boron homologations, their solution-state aggregation structures remain unresolved. In this work, a rapid-injection NMR study was undertaken to characterize unstabilized α-halo lithium carbenoids at –105 °C. 13C–6Li scalar coupling established direct carbon–lithium connectivity, and DOSY NMR revealed that the lithium carbenoids exist as monomeric species solvated by THF.

title: Benchmarking thermoelectric property extraction from scientific text
abstract: We compare five methods for extracting thermoelectric property records from paragraphs of the literature (regular expressions, the ChemDataExtractor thermoelectric parsers, MaterialsBERT named-entity recognition with rule-based linking, a single-prompt large language model (LLM) and an LLM agent) on one corpus of 311 papers with one scoring rule, with all methods frozen before the 200-paragraph test sample was annotated. A record counts as correct only if property, value, temperature and material all match the gold standard.

title: Extending the Life of High-Voltage LiCoO2 Phone Cells in Hot Climates: An Evidence-Calibrated Assessment of Electrolyte and Cathode Improvements
abstract: High-voltage lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO 2 ) phone cells age faster in heat, yet public data on their life in hot climates are scarce. This study estimates how much a published electrolyte additive package (nitrile, LiDFOB or LiPO 2 F 2 , TMSPi,low FEC) and further cathode stabilisation (trace Ti–Mg–Al doping, surface coating, single-crystalparticles) could extend the life of an iPhone 17-type cell (3,692 mAh, 4.50 V, rated ≥1,000 cycles to 80%).

title: Sulfur-Coordinated Iron Overcomes Stability Limitations in Atomically Dispersed Metal-Nitrogen-Carbon Catalysts for CO 2 Electrolysis
abstract: Metal-nitrogen-carbon (M-N x -C) catalysts are a versatile platform for electrochemical CO 2 reduction catalysis, yet the limited durability of Fe-containing active sites at industrially relevant current densities remains an obstacle. Here we report a synthesis strategy that selectively incorporates sulfur into the coordination environment of atomically dispersed iron centers within a dual-metal Fe-S y /Ni-N x -C catalyst, yielding sulfur rich coordinated Fe active sites, represented by a Fe-S 5 model, alongside predominantly Ni-N x coordinated active sites.

title: Alignment and directional ionic transport in liquid-crystalline and related ordered soft electrolytes: a 25-study evidence map with an architecture-aware comparability audit
abstract: Directional ionic transport is widely reported in liquid-crystalline and related ordered soft electrolytes, but a conductivity ratio has no fixed meaning unless the alignment, transport axis, specimen history, and measurement architecture are reported together. This public-source evidence map examined 25 primary studies across ionic liquid crystals, liquid-crystalline polymers, proton-conductive networks, gels, and related ordered soft materials.

title: Spectral Identification of Hydrino Compound Fe2O3:H2(1/4) by Five Complementary Spectroscopies R. L. Mills and W.R. Hagen
abstract: Mills solves the hydrogen atom and molecule in exact equations that give the experimental observables of both. Uniquely, Mills predicts that in addition to the reciprocal integer squared excited-state electronic energy states of atomic hydrogen, hydrogen possesses integer squared electronic energy levels corresponding to 1/p replacing n in the Rydberg formula, corresponding so-called hydrino state of hydrogen.

title: Aqueous SEC–MALS Characterization of Hydrophilic Azolium-Based Poly(ionic liquid)s in Their Native Halide Form
abstract: The molar-mass characterization of hydrophilic poly(ionic liquid)s (PILs) is challenging due to strong polymer–column interactions and low refractive-index contrast, which limit detector sensitivity. To address these limitations, we analyzed five imidazolium-based PILs using both aqueous and organic (THF/LiTFSI) size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) with polystyrene calibration or multi-angle light-scattering detection (SEC-MALS). In THF/LiTFSI, the low dn/dc values compromised sensitivity, hindering reliable molar-mass determination.

title: Single-protein diffusion in micrometer-size vesicles is governed by viscosity, surface charge, and membrane interactions
abstract: Giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) are a powerful model system for studying protein dynamics in cell-sized compartments with a precisely tunable physicochemical environment. Here, we apply Single-Molecule Displacement Mapping (SMdM) to quantify how luminal viscosity, ionic strength, membrane lipid composition, and protein surface charge of soluble proteins govern intraluminal single-molecule diffusion. Increasing viscosity led to a predictable decrease in the diffusion coefficient. However, spatially resolved diffusion measurements reveal reduced protein mobility near the membrane, suggesting additional membrane-proximal interactions not captured by particle-based simulations. We observe long-range (~1 um) effects of membrane charge on protein mobility that extend well beyond classical Debye screening, which may reflect shape fluctuations of the GUV membrane. For the membrane-associated protein LactC2, we resolve two distinct diffusing populations within a single vesicle, corresponding to free and membrane-bound states. Our workflow provides a quantitative framework for probing single-protein mobility in vesicle-based synthetic cells. These results advance our understanding of how molecular crowding and transient membrane interactions shape protein diffusion within cell-sized compartments, with possible implications for metabolic organization.

title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR
abstract: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended the analysis from backbone to side-chain nuclear spins, thus enabling the atom-resolved identification of short-range contacts between the calixarene ligands and methyl or aromatic groups of the protein surface, and revealing how these interactions refine the electrostatically driven association within different lysine-rich motifs. This approach provides a comprehensive description of how the macrocycles recognize and bind the target protein, offering a basis for the rational design of ligands capable of modulating protein function.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Policy Watch: EPA action on data center turbines prompts concerns
abstract: A weekly roundup of policy news in the chemical arena and beyond

title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
abstract: We develop an end-to-end framework for assessing a quantum-computing application in industrial materials science: the screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for SOFCs and SOECs. We formulate the materials problem in terms of interface observables including oxygen-vacancy formation energies, vacancy migration barriers, and electronic conductivity. We describe how these observables can be obtained using a diagrammatic GW-based embedding, either GW+DMFT or self-energy embedding theory (SEET), applied to a DFT-screened shortlist. The atomistic electrode/electrolyte interface defines the electronic structure problem from which the correlated impurity models are constructed. Quantum impurity solvers would provide the finite-temperature impurity Green's functions required by the embedding. The computational challenges that classical solvers may encounter as the interacting active space grows, together with the polynomial scaling of quantum Hamiltonian simulation for efficiently represented discretized models, open an opportunity for quantum advantage. We identify the benchmarks needed to assess this opportunity through convergence of vacancy and migration energetics and comparison with the best applicable classical solvers. We provide illustrative logical qubit counts and identify the thermal state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated-solve costs needed for a complete resource assessment. We connect microscopic observables to macroscopic engineering metrics using a continuum model for mixed ionic--electronic conducting oxygen electrodes that couples oxygen surface exchange, solid-state oxygen transport, electrode microstructure, and finite electrode thickness. Finally, we estimate the potential worldwide business value of improved electrode materials under SOFC and SOEC deployment scenarios informed by public technical targets and electrolyser deployment data.

title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
abstract: Institutions that deploy large language models in regulated settings often need technical evidence of responsible AI practices before approving a deployment. COMPL-AI provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act that organises this evidence under six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, twelve of which current benchmarks can measure. The benchmark suites that produce this evidence are typically operated from a command line, while the staff who approve deployments are non-engineers. We present VERA, an open-source self-hosted dashboard deployed to facilitate responsible AI processes within a large European bank. A reviewer selects a model and runs public benchmarks against it. VERA scores the twelve requirements that current benchmarks can measure and instruments the energy consumed by each evaluation, adding run-level evidence for environmental impact. We run four served open-weight models through the requirement pipeline, and the dashboard displays a score for each measurable requirement. A within-subject study then compares how participants read these benchmark results: from the raw output files in one condition, and through the VERA dashboard in the other. The dashboard reduced the time needed to perform the responsible AI assessment, reducing the time required from 56 seconds using raw files to 30 seconds using our dashboard, on average. Our dashboard scored highly (4.36 out of 5) on usefulness in the survey conducted within the organization. The dashboard and the study material are released publicly to promote replicability and reproducibility in different organisational contexts.

title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
abstract: Understanding and controlling how systems evolve is central to science and engineering, where many problems require reasoning about complete trajectories. Existing approaches typically learn local dynamics or generate trajectories, but objectives constructed from individual transitions can miss dependencies across time, while generative models do not necessarily provide a tractable objective for evaluating and optimizing arbitrary paths. We study $\textit{action learning}$, the problem of recovering a stochastic action from trajectory observations, yielding a common objective for reasoning about dynamical systems. We introduce $\textbf{LEAP}$ ($\textbf{L}$earned $\textbf{E}$nergy on $\textbf{A}$ction $\textbf{P}$aths), which anchors the unknown action to a tractable reference process and learns the remaining correction by comparing observed trajectories with reference trajectories. This construction yields a differentiable objective on path space that can capture both local dynamical structure and nonadditive dependencies across time. Once learned, the same action can be flexibly reused for path ranking and inference, mechanism steering, constrained optimization and sampling. Across stochastic physical systems, many-body orbital dynamics and molecular simulations, LEAP recovers underlying dynamics, captures dependencies across time and enables transfer across inference objectives and physical conditions. We show that $\textit{action learning}$ is a promising framework for turning trajectory observations into reusable objectives for scientific inference and control.

title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%). Production log analysis over the deployment period shows a 29.5% reduction in weekly API cost. We report this as descriptive deployment evidence. This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.

title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.

title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
abstract: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families. In this paper we extend the applicability of machine learning to novel and understudied materials through the PYTHIA (Probabilistic Yet Transferable Hierarchical Interaction Architecture) framework. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. The resulting model is used as a surrogate for a Bayesian Optimization scheme. To showcase the robustness of the framework, we applied it to the investigation of adsorption and defect optimization of two distinct systems. Not only were we able to correctly and efficiently identify the optimal adsorption sites of even complex a

title: Phosphorus-Mediated Optical Defect Engineering in Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Defect engineering of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) offers a versatile strategy for tailoring their optical properties through localized chemical modification. However, expanding the range of accessible defect chemistries beyond established oxygen- and aryl-based functionalities remains an important challenge. Here, we report a straightforward, light-driven strategy for introducing phosphorus-derived defects into (6,5)-enriched SWCNTs using triphenylphosphine (TPP) and a photosensitizing dye.

title: High-Valent Copper(III) Cyanide Tetramer Stabilized by Trifluoromethyl Ligands and its Multifaceted Reactivity
abstract: High-valent neutral copper(III) complexes are highly elusive species with strong Lewis acidic properties and high effective nuclear charge. Herein, an unprecedented copper(III) cyanide [Cu(CF3)2(CN)]4 stabilized in a tetrameric square-like scaffold with bridging cyanide ligands was isolated and fully characterized in the form of tetrahydrate [Cu(CF3)2(CN)(H2O)]4, including X-ray crystallography. This tetrameric scaffold is stable to Lewis bases, while the apical ligands easily undergo substitution to acetonitrile and cis-trans isomerization in the presence of acetone.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric Remote ε-Arylation/Cyclization of Yne-Indole Esters with 5-Aminopyrazoles toward Polycyclic Fused Seven-Membered Azaheterocycles
abstract: Chiral Cu-catalyzed asymmetric remote ε-arylation/cyclization of yne-indole esters with 5-aminopyrazoles is reported to construct polycyclic fused seven-membered azaheterocycles. After systematic screening of copper sources, chiral ligands, bases and temperature protocols, the optimized CuCl2/L12/DABCO system delivers products in good yields and high enantioselectivities. This transformation exhibits broad substrate compatibility, and steric/electronic effects on stereocontrol are discussed.

title: Fluoroalkynes: The Last Frontier of Organofluorine Chemistry?
abstract: Molecules containing carbon-fluorine bonds are of global importance in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and polymers and are widely studied. However, little is known about fluoroalkynes where a fluorine atom is directly bonded to a carbon atom that forms part of a carbon-carbon triple bond. Pioneering studies in the 20th century established that these compounds are typically unstable, but their chemistry has remained largely unexplored to date.

title: A Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Zero-Plating Fast Charging of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Real-Time Electrochemical State Estimation and Barrier-Riding Optimal Control
abstract: Extreme fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is critically limited by internal lithium plating at the negative electrode-separator interface, driving rapid degradation and thermal hazards. Real-time mitigation is fundamentally impeded because the interfacial plating overpotential (ηplating) is inaccessible to non-invasive sensors, leaving conventional protocols blind to metallic lithium deposition.

title: Synthesis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural using sulfonated calix[4]arene in brine and rapid reaction monitoring with micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography
abstract: The acid-catalyzed dehydration of D-(−)-fructose into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) and side product levulinic acid (LA) in saturated aqueous sodium chloride was investigated with 1 H quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (qNMR) and micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC). The highest isolated HMF yield of 32.7 ± 5.4 % was obtained with 2 mol% sulfonated calix[4]arene (sC4A) from 0.3 M fructose over 4 hours at 140 °C showing modestly improved performance over p -toluenesulfonic acid, methanesulfonic acid, p-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid, sulfuric acid and…

title: Charge-Transfer-State Descriptors from Donor–Acceptor Interfaces Enable Improved Prediction of Indoor Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
abstract: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices have attracted significant attention as lightweight, flexible, and solution-processable alternatives to conventional solar cells. In this work, a novel computational workflow was developed to generate donor–acceptor interfacial adducts for non-fullerene acceptor (NFA)-based indoor OPV systems and to investigate their charge-transfer (CT) characteristics using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations.

title: Improved Prediction of Mössbauer Quadrupole Splitting at High and Low Temperatures with a Quantum Chemical Ensemble Approach
abstract: Mössbauer spectroscopy is a key method for characterizing the electronic structures of iron compounds. The resulting Mössbauer parameters show a well-established temperature dependence. For quantum chemical calculations that are often used to aid in the interpretation of Mössbauer spectra, this poses a major challenge: they commonly employ a single, rigid equilibrium structure that is assumed to deliver good results for low temperatures up to ca. 80 K. In this work, we reveal this approach to be a rather severe approximation.

title: Influence of Divalent Cations on the Mechanical Properties of DNA Origami Six-Helix Bundles
abstract: The mechanical behavior of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) is governed by both design parameters and ionic environment, yet their coupled effects remain poorly understood. Here, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based contour analysis is used to quantify the persistence length (Lp), contour length (Lc), and end-to-end distance (Ree) of DON six-helix bundles (6HBs) with different staple crossover densities.

title: Programming of Dissipative Networks and Transient Vesicles Using Intrinsic Kinetic Discrimination of Thiol Oxidation
abstract: Programmable dissipative systems that mimic life’s ability to execute timed functions—such as apoptosis triggered by inherent reactivity contrasts—remain a fundamental challenge, as most synthetic designs lack the kinetic complexity to orchestrate multi-step, autonomous sequences. Here, we introduce a synthetic dissipative network in which the intrinsic oxidation kinetics of mono- and dithiols serve as an embedded reaction window to program a cascade of thiol-thioester exchange reactions.

title: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF AROMATICITY IN TAUTOMERIC EQUILIBRIA
abstract: Tautomerism, the interconversion of small molecules via proton and π-electron shifts, poses a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as different tautomers can exhibit distinct physicochemical properties and receptor-binding profiles, while computational approaches have been widely applied to predict tautomeric equilibria, most methods often overlook electronic properties such as aromaticity, which are critical to molecular stability.

title: HF· · ·H2S Hydrogen-Bonded Clusters as a Model for Probing Subtle Cooperative Effects
abstract: Hydrogen-bond (HB) cooperativity is usually analysed for whole networks, and its variation between individual HBs is poorly understood when strong and weak donors coexist. We resolve 126 HBs in 20 neutral cyclic (HF)m(H2S)n clusters (Nmon = m + n = 3–7). The molecular tailoring approach (MTA) at the MP2/aug-ccpVTZ level splits each in-cluster HB energy into an isolated-dimer part and a network-associated (cooperative) part. The mean MTA energies of the F–H· · ·F, F–H· · · S, S–H· · · F and S–H· · · S bonds are 9.03, 8.47, 2.57 and 2.45 kcal mol−1, respectively.

title: Chemoselective Copper(l)-Catalyzed 1,2-Reduction of Conjugated Amides by a Molecular Recognition Strategy
abstract: The selective 1,2-reduction of conjugated amides represents an elusive transformation, owing to the intrinsically low reactivity of the amide group and competing conjugate reduction. Here, we report an unprecedented copper(I)-catalyzed hydrogenation of conjugated amides that selectively furnishes allylic alcohols using molecular hydrogen as the terminal reductant.

title: Hydroxyurea synthesis using resonant acoustic mixing in ethanol
abstract: Hydroxyurea derivatives have important medicinal utility acting as enzyme inhibitors and anticancer agents. Their syntheses have, however, entailed low yielding routes employing long reaction times and toxic reagents such as phosgene. Towards sustainable and environmentally benign hydroxyurea synthesis, a one-step hydroxycarbamoylation approach is described employing resonant acoustic mixing (RAM) to expedite reactions at higher concentration. Eighteen medicinally relevant hydroxyurea were synthesized in 68-91% yields using ethanol as green solvent.

title: An [Fe32] molecular metal oxide
abstract: Reaction of [Fe16] with 3-chloropyridine results in formation of an [Fe32] cluster, whose magnetic skeleton describes interwoven triangular and square tilings, demonstrating that pre-formed molecular iron oxides can be used as starting materials to access new species. Magnetic measurements reveal competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions, resulting in significant spin frustration.

title: VHH-Bench: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Nanobody–Antigen Complex Predictions Across CDR3 Conformations
abstract: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies.

title: Precursor Formulation Redirects Phase Competition and Thermal Evolution in Silver Multinary Chalcogenide Ag-M-Ch (M = Zr, Cr, Sn, Sb) Nanocrystals
abstract: Multinary nanocrystal synthesis requires chemically dissimilar metals to enter a common framework while competing with binary crystallization and metal reduction. We examine this competition through 31 preparation records spanning nominal Ag8SnS6, Ag4Zr3S8, AgZrSe2, AgCrSe2, and Ag3SbS3 targets in an oleylamine–octadecene platform. In a matched Ag–Zr–S comparison at 240 °C for 20 min, replacing an elemental-sulfur-derived stock with trioctylphosphine sulfide redirects a dense diffraction fingerprint toward a sparse fcc-Ag-compatible series.

title: Homogeneous–Heterogeneous Hybrid Oxidation Catalysis Based on Multiple Adsorption Enabling Efficient Aerobic Amide Oxygenation
abstract: Homogeneous–heterogeneous combined catalysts, such as immobilized homogeneous catalysts and single-atom catalysts (SACs), have been developed to improve catalytic performance and practicality and elucidate catalytic mechanisms. However, achieving new catalytic functions beyond those of the individual components remains challenging. Homogeneous–heterogeneous hybrid catalysis offers a contrasting approach: homogeneous catalysts can coordinate/adsorb onto heterogeneous catalysts, allowing the two components to cooperate and potentially enable new catalytic processes for efficient molecular…

title: Non-Markovian Memory Kernels in Condensed-Phase Chemical Dynamics: From Dipole Dephasing and Conical Intersections to Spin Crossover and Radical-Pair Magnetoreception
abstract: Standard theoretical formulations of ultrafast condensed-phase molecular processes rely heavily on Markovian master equations and time-local Lindblad semigroups that assume memoryless bath relaxation (t ≫ τB). However, in viscous solvents, structured protein binding pockets, and biomolecular matrices, environmental fluctuations exhibit power-law algebraic memory tails K(t) ∝ t−µ (µ ∈ (0, 1)) where Markovian approximations break down.

title: PerMix: Algorithmic Pathway Planning for Multicomponent Halide Perovskite Synthesis
abstract: The reproducible growth of multicomponent halide perovskite single crystals depends critically on the stoichiometry of the precursor solution: even small deviations introduced during weighing or dissolution can change phase purity, defect density, and the lattice parameters of the resulting crystals. Today, recipes for such systems are still planned largely by hand in spreadsheets, which are error-prone, difficult to audit, and impractical for the compositional spaces of multicomponent solid solutions.

title: Deterministic Preparation of Intermolecular Spin States Through Collective Light Emission in Copper Porphyrin Aggregates
abstract: The coupling of electron spins in open shell systems drives formation of distinct singlet and triplet states whose transitions possess unique coherence properties relative to those of doublets. Here we show that exchange interactions couple the electron spins on neighboring Cu cations within porphyrins macrocycles that participate in aggregate formation. Following photoexcitation, we find a ‘low field’ EPR signal whose peak position and shape are reproduced by simulations of anti-ferromagnetically coupled electron spins.

title: Wigner Momentum Estimation and Sampling with Local Modes: A Second-Moment Approximation to High-Frequency Momentum Marginals
abstract: Instantaneous local Gaussian approximations assign nuclear momentum widths from the curvature of the potential at each sampled configuration. Strongly compressed bonds can consequently acquire large momentum widths even when their positions are drawn from an anharmonic path-integral ensemble. We estimate momentum covariances from pathintegral coordinates and forces in local modes that follow molecular deformations. These covariances define Gaussian approximations to high-frequency Wigner momentum marginals without evaluating a Hessian at each configuration.

title: Interstitial Oxygen and a Two-Dimensional Migration Pathway in Mo-Substituted Palmierite Ba 3 V 2−x Mo x O 8+x/2
abstract: Palmierite oxides are promising oxide-ion conductors, with conductivities exceeding those of related hexagonal perovskite derivatives. However, aliovalent Mo6+ substitution in Ba 3 V 2 O 8 has previously been demonstrated only at high substitution levels. Here, the Ba 3 V 2-x Mo x O 8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3) was investigated using X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, 51 V and 17 O solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT), and bond-valence site-energy (BVSE) calculations.

title: Predicting excess solvation in binary solvents toward green organic semiconductor processing
abstract: Replacing halogenated solvents in organic semiconductor inks benefits from binary mixtures that balance dissolution and film drying, yet mixing changes solvation beyond the pure-solvent contributions. Here, we introduce ShellEx, a three-dimensional contact-shell model distilled from openCOSMO-RS that predicts this endpoint-fixed excess solvation from force-field geometries.

title: The Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation in Quantum Chemistry: Symmetrized Riesz Exchange Kernels, Sobolev Domain Classification, and O(N4) Quasiparticle Electronic Structure across Bond Dissociation
abstract: A central challenge in ab initio electronic structure theory is capturing both short-range dynamic electron correlation (the Kato inter-electronic cusp) and long-range static multireference correlation across covalent bond dissociation without incurring the exponential O(exp N) cost of Full Configuration Interaction (FCI), the O(N⁶) cost and single-reference breakdown of Coupled Cluster Singles and Doubles (CCSD), or the one-electron self-interaction error (SIE) of Density Functional Theory (DFT).

title: Imbalanced burner heat release for enhanced ethylene yield in industrial-scale cracking furnaces
abstract: Symmetric burner arrangements with uniform heat release are the default design for cracking furnaces. However, the present study reveals that this symmetric layout leads to inferior heating conditions and reduced ethylene yields in specific coils. Therefore, an imbalanced heating strategy is proposed: side burners are grouped by location, with the fuel flow rate of Group L set to four times that of Group R while maintaining the same total fuel consumption.

title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

title: Resolving Ultrafast Carrier-to-Exciton Conversion in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals Formed from Solid-State Photochemistry
abstract: Photoinduced conversion provides an alternative pathway to form CsPbBr3 nanocrystals from their twodimensional analogues, nanoplatelets, using optical excitation in the solid phase. Although this transformation has been previously observed, it is unclear how the ultrafast dynamics of excitons in the resulting nanocrystals compare with those of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals synthesized in solution.

title: Adsorption–Absorption Polymer Purification (AAPP): A Mass Transfer Strategy for Removing Residual Monomer from Synthetic Polymers
abstract: After polymerization, synthetic polymers frequently contain residual monomers, solvents, and other low molar mass compounds that can adversely affect material properties and subsequent applications. Their removal remains challenging, as conventional purification methods such as precipitation and dialysis are often time-consuming, difficult to standardize, and generate substantial amounts of solvent waste.

title: Transferable Quasiparticle Correlation, Subtractive Multireference Embedding for Biradicaloid Ozone, and Retarded Casimir–Polder Dispersion in Multi-Electron Systems
Airborne Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) in 20 Homes Several Months After the 2023 Maui Wildfires
abstract: Exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) is associated with adverse health outcomes, including cancer. PAHs are emitted by wildfires and may persist in indoor environments following smoke events. To better understand post-wildfire PAH persistence inside residences, we sampled for 16 airborne PAHs at 20 homes in Lāhainā, Hawaiʻi, 5-7 months after the 2023 Maui wildfires, both before and after deploying an additional air purifier on top of existing indoor filtration and purification systems. Additionally, we surveyed building occupants about pollution-relevant behaviors.

title: Temperature Range
abstract: Perfectly uniform and conformal thin films of materials are routinely deposited by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) for a range of applications, especially in the semiconductor industry. The most common way to enable highly conformal deposition is to operate the CVD process in the kinetically limited temperature regime, i.e., at the lower temperature range where the deposition chemistry is active. Here, we present the unexpected finding that a conformal CVD process is also available at very high temperatures.

title: Eliminating the remaining spin contamination of MRSF-TDDFT by completing its core–virtual block
abstract: We introduce a core–virtual-complete variant of mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT), CV-MRSF, which completes the block of core-to-virtual (CV) excitations. For each CV excitation, the four determinants missing from MRSF-TDDFT are recovered by imposing exact spin adaptation, which makes every singlet and triplet spin pure and gives the proper singlet–triplet splitting of CV states without spin-pairing couplings.

title: Accelerating characterization of conformational stability for biologics in Discovery space by combining SEC‑HDX‑MS with molecular modeling
abstract: Conformational stability is a critical attribute for biologics discovery and manufacturability assessment, yet conventional approaches often require substantial material, extensive preparation, or lack sufficient structural resolution for early decision-making. Here, we present a native size-exclusion chromatography hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (SEC-HDX-MS) workflow integrated with molecular modeling to rapidly characterize conformational stability of therapeutic proteins in the discovery space.

title: Universality of Lithium Metal and Solid Electrolyte Interphase Descriptors of Coulombic Efficiency Governed by Lithium Connectivity
abstract: Coulombic efficiency (CE) is a key metric governing the cyclability of lithium metal anodes, motivating efforts to identify physicochemical descriptors that correlate with CE. Diverse descriptors spanning electrolyte thermodynamics and interphase properties have been proposed, but their interrelationships and underlying physical origins remain unclear. Here we show that, when evaluated across a consistent electrolyte set, these descriptors exhibit a common hockey-stick relationship with CE that can be unified through the mesoscale connectivity of lithium deposits.

title: Aromaticity Hidden in Magnetically Antiaromatic Macrocycles
abstract: Global paratropic ring currents give norcorrole and rosarin a familiar antiaromatic label and account for their characteristic pattern of deshielded inner and shielded outer protons. Translating that magnetic picture into a perimeter of alternating double bonds, however, assigns the occupied 𝜋 electrons to a bonding pattern that the current pathway alone does not determine. Here we ask how much of the ground-state bonding the magnetic response actually reveals.

title: What Information Is Required to Learn Molecular Pauli Potentials? A Nonlocal Descriptor Hierarchy for Orbital-Free Density Functional Theory
abstract: Practical orbital-free density functional theory (OF-DFT) for molecules remains limited by the unknown Pauli contribution to the noninteracting kinetic energy. Here, we ask what information a density representation must contain for a machine-learned (ML) Pauli potential to drive an orbital-free Euler solution toward its Kohn–Sham (KS) reference. For C2H2, a frozen KS-derived Pauli-potential oracle yields an OF energy within 3.15 mHa of the KS reference, establishing the numerical accuracy attainable within the chosen finite representation.

title: mzView : visualizing mass spectrometry data in the browser
abstract: Routine inspection of raw mass spectrometry data is limited to installed desktop software which often needs high memory, security updates, compatible operating system, and hard-drive space. Existing web-based tools require uploading raw data files to a server. To address this, we introduce mzView, a zero-installation web application featuring client-side modules for visualizing mass spectrometry data files covering Data Dependent Acquisition (DDA), Data Independent Acquisition (DIA), Imaging, and Ion-mobility acquisitions. mzView supports mzML, imzML, MSP, Bruker (.d) file formats.

title: Disentangling Between-Target and Within-Target Signal in PPI Benchmarking
abstract: Pooled correlation, the metric usually reported when predicting mutation effects on protein–protein binding affinity (ΔΔG), mixes two different capabilities: placing targets on a common binding scale and ranking mutations correctly within a target. We formulate an exact between-/within-target covariance decomposition for PPI ΔΔG benchmarking, r = C_B + C_W, and apply it to matched, provenance-filtered evaluation sets.

title: Direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F Cross-Coupling of Methylpyridines with Aryl Fluorides
abstract: Direct C(sp3)–H functionalization of methylpyridines is intrinsically challenging. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, silylboronate-mediated heterobenzylation of methylpyridines with aryl fluorides. The combination of a silylboronate and KOtBu enables direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to structurally diverse azaarylmethanes.

title: Tunable Emission from Quasi-2D Perovskites via Electrospinning
abstract: Quasi-2D Ruddlesden-Popper halide perovskites are promising materials for light-emitting applications. They comprise corner-sharing metal-halide octahedra separated by bulky, insulating organic spacers and exhibit tunable bandgaps by varying the number of octahedral layers, n . Isolating a single n -phase within a film remains challenging, with spin-coated films generally containing a broad distribution of n phases. Their emission is dominated by the largest n -number present due to energy funneling towards narrow bandgap phases.

title: Lewis Acid-Activated Bathophenanthroline Photoredox System for Chlorine Radical-Mediated C(sp³)–H Alkylation
abstract: Despite major advances in photoredox catalysis, photocatalysts capable of oxidizing substrates with E ox > +2.0 V vs SCE remain limited. Herein, we report that a Lewis acid-activated bathophenanthroline (bphen) photoredox system with ZrCl 4 enables intermolecular single-electron oxidation of chloride ( E ox = +2.03 V vs SCE). Under visible-light irradiation, this system promotes Giese-type alkylation of electron-deficient alkenes with a broad range of C(sp 3 )–H donors through chlorine radical-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT).

title: Quantum Graph-Theoretic Docking of Multiple Ligands Targeting CMG Helicase: Analysis of Interaction Patterns and Ideal Ligand Composition
abstract: Molecular docking and compound screening can overlook and biochemically relevant binding configurations of molecules, limiting the ability to identify true functional poses of potential drug candidates. To address this, we apply the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to improve the evaluation of target–ligand interaction patterns. As a proof of concept, we focus on the CDC45–MCM2-7–GINS (CMG) helicase, which is essential for DNA replication and represents a potential therapeutic target in cancer due to mutant KRas-induced vulnerabilities in the CMG and its MCM hexameric core.

title: Risk-Priced Radio Resources for In-Line Spectroscopy and Reaction Monitoring in Chemical Plants
abstract: In-line spectroscopy now carries the chemical plant’s quality decisions over shared industrial wireless links, yet the schedulers distributing those links optimize throughput, fairness or delay and are blind to chemistry: an MIR quantification stream survives compression, while a runaway precursor confined to a narrow wavenumber window disappears with it. We present ChemRAN, a chemistry-aware orchestration framework for wireless process analytical technology networks.

title: Multi-Agent Scheduling of Instrument-Time for High-Throughput Palladium-Catalysed Cross-Coupling
abstract: NMR time and a shared liquid-handling robot are scarce, noisy and only partially observable, so the practical question is which experiment to run next on which instrument. Existing reaction-optimisation benchmarks measure budgets in experiments rather than instrumenthours, and they learn chemical feasibility only by paying for infeasible runs. We present CHASE, a centralised-training decentralised-execution scheduler with three coupled modules: a belief encoder (PEB) infers per-instrument throughput and channel health from local event histories and exchanges only low-bandwidth summaries; a…

title: Enhancing Ethylene Yields and Energy Efficiency in Industrial Cracking Furnaces via Spatial Heat-Flux Optimization
abstract: Steam cracking furnaces are conventionally operated by raising the coil outlet temperature (COT) via increased fuel input, yet this approach yields diminishing selectivity gains while accelerating coking. Using a high-fidelity 3D coupled furnace–reactor model consistent with industrial design parameters, we demonstrate that COT is not the primary control lever. Instead, at a fixed total heat input, the spatial distribution of heat flux along the coil axis governs ethylene yields and cracking severity.

title: Mass Balance-based Computational Frameworks for the
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic contaminants widely 20 detected in aquatic environments. Conventional wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are major 21 emission sources that discharge PFAS via effluent and the land application of biosolids, yet they 22 are ineffective in removing PFAS. Understanding PFAS distribution and transformation in 23 WWTPs is important for the development and integration of PFAS remediation technologies.

title: Mediator-Assisted Energy Release Enabled by Positional Isomerism in Norbornadiene/Quadricyclane Systems
abstract: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems store solar energy in metastable photoisomers and release it on demand through triggered back-conversion. Here, we show that mixtures of MOST compounds enable a distinct energy-release strategy in which one component mediates the activation of another. Using methoxyphenyl-substituted norbornadiene/quadricyclane (NBD/QC) positional isomers, we show by in situ photoelectrochemical infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (PEC-IRRAS) and density functional theory (DFT) that substituent position shifts the electrochemical onset potential by up to 0.6 V…

title: Polyamide Reverse Osmosis Membranes Are Less Crosslinked Than Previously Thought
abstract: Polyamide membranes are central to industrial separations, including desalination and water treatment. They are typically described as comprising crosslinked and linear units. Molecular dynamics simulations and topological analysis find branched units to be similar to or more prevalent than crosslinked units, and ignoring them can mischaracterize polyamide membranes.

title: Substituted Catechols as H-Bonding Organocatalysts in Conjugated Addition Reactions of (Hetero-)Arenes to Nitroolefins
abstract: Hydrogen-bond donor organocatalysts based on thioureas, silanols, amidines and diols have been studied in-depth. However, catechols – as prototypical diol catalysts – are comparatively underexplored despite their structural simplicity, straightforward accessibility, and tunability. Here, we systematically investigate substituted catechols as hydrogen-bond donor catalysts for the conjugate addition of indoles to nitroolefins. Screening of the catechol substitution pattern identified 4bromocatechol as the most active derivative.

title: Accelerating Mechanistic Understanding and Prediction of Chemical Selectivity with Foundation Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Selectivity in chemical reactions is often dictated by small energetic differences between competing transition states of less than 2 kcal mol -1 . Computational predictions of selectivity for organic and organometallic reactions must reach these levels of quantitative accuracy, while simultaneously navigating the mechanistic and conformational complexity involved. Here, we assess the suitability of foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for this task.

title: Ab-initio Exploration of Structural, Electronic, Optical and Transport Properties of Rb2Te Photocathodes
abstract: Using state-of-the-art first-principles calculations based on hybrid density functional theory, we investigate the key material properties governing photoemission in Rb2Te for photocathode applications. Multiple crystalline phases of Rb2Te are examined, among which the α-and ω-phases are found to be both dynamically and mechanically stable. These phases exhibit exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivities of 0.27 Wm−1K−1 and 1.61 Wm−1K−1 for the α-and ω-phases, respectively.

title: Contact-electro-catalytic degradation of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid using PTFE
abstract: This study introduces an ultrasound-powered contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) method for degrading 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (HBA) using polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) microparticles. Under neutral conditions, the system achieved over 99% HBA degradation in aqueous solutions. Mechanistic analysis confirms that hydroxyl radicals act as the primary oxidants. HBA degradation proceeds via primary hydroxylation and secondary decarboxylation pathway. The effects of acidic and alkaline conditions were investigated, demonstrating the non-innocent role of counter ions.

title: Spontaneous Curvature and Differential Leaflet Tension Are Additive Drives for Outward Membrane Budding
abstract: Two recent models derive outward plasma-membrane budding from different starting points. Mahapatra, Malingen and Rangamani treat a microparticle as a Helfrich membrane in which phosphatidylserine exposed on the outer leaflet imposes a local spontaneous curvature over a prescribed domain, coupled to cortex linkers modelled as springs. Our own treatment derives an energetic threshold from the differential tension between leaflets generated by a net transbilayer lipid flux, with vesicle size as an output rather than an input.

title: Formate Electrosynthesis via Selective Ethylene Glycol Oxidation on Ni-Modified CeO2−x/NF
abstract: Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) offers a route to replace the anodic oxygen evolution reaction while converting ethylene glycol into value-added products. Here, electrodeposited CeO2−x//NF and Ni-modified CeO2−x/NF were evaluated for EGOR in alkaline electrolyte. Ni modification markedly enhanced the polarization response, enabling a current density of 100 mA cm-2 at 1.61 V vs RHE without iR compensation, approximately 97 mV lower than that of the parent CeO2−x/NF electrode at the same current density.

title: Synergistic effects of biochar and vegetation on microplastic and nanoplastic removal from stormwater runoff in bioretention systems
abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are emerging contaminants in stormwater runoff, posing potential ecological and human health risks. Bioretention systems offer promising nature-based stormwater treatment, yet their performance remains highly variable. Biochar, particularly post-processed biochar, has demonstrated strong potential for contaminant removal; however, its effects on MNP removal, leachate quality, and plant performance in green infrastructure remain poorly understood.

title: Disclosing the Effect of Activation on the Micro- and Meso-structure of Activated Carbons with SANS and Gas Sorption
abstract: Tuning the performance of a porous material is a major leap towards more efficient use and reduced production costs. The performance of activated carbons (ACs) in applications such as catalysis, energy storage, and environmental remediation is closely linked to their micro- and meso-structure, side to their surface chemistry. However, their intrinsic disorder and large panel of possible synthetic treatments bring to a complex structure that standard analysis technique only are not capable to depict entirely.

title: Outpacing H-Phosphonate Oxidation: Enantioconvergent Deborylative Synthesis of α-Stereogenic Alkyl Phosphonates
abstract: The growing biomedical relevance of α-stereogenic alkyl phosphonates, such as their use in enhancing the metabolic stability of oligonucleotide therapeutics, motivates versatile approaches to their asymmetric synthesis. The enantioconvergent coupling of C(sp3) building blocks and H-phosphonates offers a straightforward synthetic disconnection. Herein we report the first asymmetric deborylative C(sp3)–P coupling, harnessing the synthetic modularity of alkylboron reagents to streamline access to structurally diverse, enantioenriched α-stereogenic alkyl phosphonates.

title: Development of 3D-Printed Photoreactors for Medicinal Chemistry Applications
abstract: 3D-Printing has revolutionised the landscape of life sciences by enabling the rapid and affordable creation of bespoke equipment. The adaptation and design of light, cheap and easy to use photoredox reactors, where temperature control is introduced by compressed air flow, has allowed our laboratories to access a standardised and reproducible setup for all photoredox experiments.

title: Calcium Poly(heptazine imide): Reproducible Synthesis for Structural Analysis, Mechanism of CO 2 Uptake, and Evaluation of Photocatalytic CO 2 - to-CO Conversion
abstract: The framework material, calcium poly(heptazine imide) or CaPHI, is reportedly capable for CO 2 absorption, although harsh conditions from literature synthesis method result in low and unpredictable yield that hinders evaluation of its applicability for CO 2 capture and conversion (CCC). This work presents a synthesis procedure for CaPHI with cross-laboratory reproducibility and scalable to 100s mg by employing a CaCl 2 -based eutectic as synthesis medium.

title: Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks with Heteropore-Tuned Compact Motifs for Boosting Spin-Spin Interactions
abstract: The rich porosity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) renders them abundant mass transport channels and easily accessible active sites. However, relatively low compact skeletons of COFs are unfavorable for in-plane and out-of-plane electron spin coupling. Herein, we report a new π-extended polyheterocyclic aromatic derivative by fusing three 2,3-dimethylpyrazine moieties to a triphenylene core, which serves as a D3h-symmetric hexatopic monomer to undergo Knoevenagel condensation smoothly with linear dialdehyde aromatics, forming a novel type of two-dimensional vinylene-linked COFs.

title: Polymorphism, Crystal Habit and Intermolecular Contact Topology in Benzothiazine Derivatives: A Comparative Hirshfeld Surface Analysis of Seven Crystal Structures
abstract: Seven deposited benzothiazine crystal structures (CCDC 1835802, 1835803, 1964377–1964379, and 2102851–2102852) were reanalysed to distinguish differences in periodic crystal structures from crystal habit and positional disorder. Eight independent molecular environments were evaluated with fragment-based Hirshfeld surfaces and element-resolved contact contributions in Multiwfn. Convergence was assessed at grid spacings of 0.20 and 0.15 Bohr and with crystal-environment clusters extending to 4 and 6 Å.

title: Low-Energy Electron Attachment to Catechin Sulphate
abstract: Low-energy electron (LEE) attachment can initiate molecular fragmentation through temporary negative ion states, with autodetachment competing against nuclear motion toward dissociation. Here, we apply an improved local complex potential time-dependent wavepacket (LCP-TDWP) workflow to catechin sulphate, a metabolically relevant catechin conjugate for which, to our knowledge, a dedicated dissociative electron attachment (DEA) study has not been reported.

title: Ionic router: a shared acidic pivot swaps one salt bridge for another, encoding activation state at non-homologous positions in class B1 and class A GPCRs
abstract: We report the first instance in a class B1 G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) of a charged residue that exchanges one state-specific salt bridge for another, and the first evidence that this arrangement recurs at non-homologous positions in two receptor classes. In the human glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), E408, generic number 8.49x49, pairs with R348 (6.37x37) in 5 of 5 scorable inactive structures and 0 of 52 active, and with R176 (2.46x46) in 42 of 52 active structures and 0 of 6 inactive.

title: When Can an Off-Cycle Reservoir Raise a Catalyst’s Turnover Number?
abstract: Off-cycle species are typically considered detrimental to catalytic activity; however, a dormant form can also extend catalyst lifetime. This study shows under which conditions a reversible off-cycle reservoir can increase the turnover number (TON) of a homogeneous catalyst. When both turnover and all deactivation steps are first order in catalyst, branching remains constant over time and the reservoir only holds the catalyst in a dormant state, the distribution of turnovers per catalyst does not change, regardless of the number of reservoirs.

title: Ice Deposition of Water Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry at Cryogenic Temperatures
abstract: Water gas cluster ion beams (GCIBs) are increasingly used in cryogenic secondary ion mass spectrometry (cryo-SIMS) to improve the detection of biomolecules while preserving their molecular integrity. However, the effects of water cluster primary ion (PI) beams on cryogenically cooled surfaces are not yet fully understood. Here, we demonstrate that continuous bombardment with (H 2 O) n + GCIBs can induce ice deposition, which competes with sputtering and can ultimately obscure the underlying sample, thus compromising depth profiling and molecular analysis.

title: High-Throughput Combinatorial Screening of Refractory Amorphous Alloys for Fusion Capillary Systems via a Calibrated First-Principles Continuum-Thermodynamic Model
abstract: Liquid metal divertors utilizing Capillary Porous Systems (CPS) represent a critical armor technology for handling extreme heat fluxes (> 10–20 MW/m2) in magnetic confinement fusion. However, conventional crystalline refractory matrices suffer from liquid-metal-induced corrosion along grain boundaries, thermal embrittlement, and grain coarsening. Amorphous metallic alloys eliminate grain boundaries, but identifying high-temperature glass formers remains computationally prohibitive via density functional theory or molecular dynamics.

title: Radical Anion of Oxalate Esters: Electrochemical and EPR Investigations
abstract: The oxalic acid/oxalate family is an instrumental C 2 platform for a circular carbon economy strategy. That molecule is the first and simplest of the C‒C bonded products obtained from CO 2 , and production technologies are already available, assisted by renewable electrons or from biomass. Exploiting this family of compounds as C 2 synthons through reductive C‒C couplings into value-added carbon skeletons is a promising opportunity.

title: Reliability of Short Molecular Dynamics Runs as Screening Labels: Noise Ceilings, Time Dependence and Adaptive Replicate Allocation
abstract: High-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) produces the labels on which electrolyte screening and machine-learning models are built, but each label comes from one short, noisy run whose value still depends on the simulated time. We quantify their reliability, and how to spend a simulation budget given it, on HTP-MD, the largest public set of polymer electrolyte trajectories (6,137 runs of 5 ns and 133 of 50 ns).

title: Patterning Conductive Aluminium onto Temperature Sensitive Polymers and Tattoo Paper at Room Temperature and Pressure
abstract: Currently patterning conductive metal onto thermally fragile substrates remains hindered by the necessary processing conditions required. Aluminium is an attractive conductor for printed electronics, being non-toxic, low cost, having high abundance, while providing excellent electrical conductivity. Here, we report the direct deposition of conductive aluminium lines onto a selection of heat sensitive substrates; namely dissolvable tattoo paper, and a Polyborosiloxane (PBS)/Sylgard blend substrate at room temperature and atmospheric pressure using an atmospheric-pressure plasma jet (APPJ) and…

title: Cerium Photoredox-Catalyzed Ring Expansion of Cyclic Allylic Alcohols
abstract: Medium-sized aliphatic rings are underrepresented in drug discovery despite their advantageous balance of rigidity and flexibility. Existing synthetic limitations hinder broader exploration of this valuable chemical space. This work presents a general and efficient method for the one- and two-carbon ring expansion of 5- and 6-membered allylic alcohols to larger cyclic ketones using cerium-based photoredox catalysis.

title: Artificial Cells with a Cytoskeleton from Synthetic Self-Replicating Molecules
abstract: Living cells couple molecular replication and cytoskeletal assembly to changes in shape and mechanical stability, but reconstructing this relationship in synthetic compartments remains challenging. Here, we confine self-replicating supramolecular fibers within giant polymer lipid hybrid vesicle-based artificial cells. Seeded replicator growth produces luminal fiber networks and deforms the surrounding membrane into spindle-like morphologies, with fiber and membrane interactions controlled by membrane composition and fiber glycation.

title: Rigor & Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Best Practices for Kinetic Studies
abstract: Kinetic measurements can support or falsify mechanistic hypotheses in electrocatalysis, but only when rates reflect intrinsic catalytic behavior and models separate kinetic information from experimental artifacts and interfacial complexity. This perspective presents best practices for acquiring and interpreting electrocatalytic kinetic data, including mitigating artifacts arising from transport, ohmic losses, catalyst restructuring, contamination, and incomplete product accounting.

title: Enthalpy-Driven Design Rules for Multi-Shell Multimetallic Nanoparticles
abstract: Multimetallic nanoparticles (NPs) offer access to a vast compositional and architectural design space, yet controlled formation of core-shell and multi-shell architectures rapidly becomes unpredictable as compositional complexity increases. As a result, architectural outcomes are often regarded as system-specific and governed primarily by kinetic effects. Here, we identify a unifying thermodynamic principle that governs shell formation in multimetallic NPs based on binary mixing enthalpies and phase behaviour.

title: Catalytic N -Cbz Deprotection of Amino Acids and Dipeptides over Spherical SiliaCat Pd(0)
abstract: Investigation of hydrogenolytic removal of N -benzyloxycarbonyl ( N -Cbz) protecting groups from amino acid and dipeptide derivatives mediated by spherical SiliaCat Pd(0) under mild conditions using an H 2 -filled balloon allowed to optimize reaction parameters including solvent composition, substrate concentration, Pd loading, temperature, and catalyst particle size.

title: Second-generation tau PET tracer in situ binding assessed with fluorescence imaging
abstract: Brain positron emission tomography (PET) imaging is a valuable tool which allows visualization of the pathological structures inside the living patients’ brains. While amyloid-β PET tracers have been in use with Alzheimer’s disease patients in clinics, tau PET tracers have still not entered the clinical routine. Second-generation tau PET tracers have been developed with the aim to overcome the limitations of the first-generation tau PET tracers, such as low sensitivity and off-target binding.

title: Methyl-Induced Hydrophobicity and Electronically Tuned Copper Nanocluster COF for Highly Selective Nitrate to Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (eNO3-RR) offers a promising route for sustainable ammonia production while mitigating nitrate pollution. Yet high NH3 selectivity remains challenging owing to proton-coupled multi-electron transfer pathways and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report a trinuclear Cu nanocluster-based covalent organic framework (CuMePh) featuring methylfunctionalized π-conjugated extended porous framework that provides a molecular-level strategy for modifying the interfacial wettability and electronic environment of the catalytic framework.

title: Gold-Mediated Cascade Cyclization on-route to the Total Synthesis of (−)‑Presilphiperfolan-1-ol
abstract: We report a concise and convergent total synthesis of (−)-presilphiperfolan-1-ol, a highly strained tricyclic sesquiterpene bearing five contiguous stereocenters. Central to our strategy is a gold(I)-catalyzed cascade cyclization of a silyl enol ether containing an enyne motif, which simultaneously constructs the fused tricyclo[5.3.1.04,8]undecane core and sets three remote stereocenters.

title: Water-Model Dependence of Absolute Binding Free Energies across the Bromodomain Family
abstract: The choice of explicit water model may affect absolute binding free energy (ABFE) predictions for bromodomains, whose conserved acetyl-lysine pockets contain structured waters. We assembled a benchmark of ten distinct bromodomain–ligand complexes with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamics and compared four TIP-family water models, TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, and TIP7P, using a common alchemical protocol. TIP3P gave the lowest point-estimate mean unsigned error (MUE), 1.56 kcal mol−1, against 1.89–2.11 kcal mol−1 for the other models, at the lowest cost.

title: Automated DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis on Magnetic Anion Exchange Resin
abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) access vast chemical spaces for drug discovery, but split-and-pool DEL synthesis remains the sole and very manual portion of the DEL workflow. Here, we automate DEL construction using diethylaminoethyl-functionalized weak anion exchange (WAX) magnetic resin and a KingFisher Apex particle-handling instrument. DNA encoding occurs in solution, followed by selective immobilization of DNA conjugates under low-salt conditions that exclude > 95% of unused encoding oligonucleotides. On-DNA chemistry then proceeds using the WAX resin-adsorbed "WAX-ON" DNA substrate in neat organic solvent. The platform supports amide formation, reductive amination, copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition, and Fmoc removal. Automated bead transfer enables iterative reaction and washing cycles. We synthesized two-cycle 9,216-member DELs from 96 Fmoc-protected amino acids and 96 carboxylic acids. Control selections reproducibly enriched the carbonic anhydrase ligand sulfamoylbenzoic acid. Magnetic WAX-ON DEL synthesis is compatible with diverse chemistries and uses the same instrumentation to automate end-to-end DEL preparation and affinity screening.

title: De novo macrocyclic peptide discovery produces potent class A GPCR ligands with diverse pharmacology
abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent one of the largest protein families of therapeutic importance, as over one third of all currently approved drugs target GPCRs. A growing proportion of GPCR drugs are peptides. However, class A GPCRs (over 80% of clinically studied targets) are underexploited as peptide targets, presumably since their only structured domain is the core, seven-helix, integral membrane fold presenting a limited solvent-exposed surface area. Screening libraries of de novo macrocyclic peptides have allowed for the targeting of otherwise intractable proteins, but their potential to generate selective ligands for class A GPCRs has not been demonstrated. Here, we used random nonstandard peptides integrated discovery (RaPID) to identify de novo macrocyclic peptide ligands targeting the chemokine receptor CXCR4. CXCR4 regulates cell migration, immune surveillance, and inflammation, making it an important therapeutic target for multiple diseases. We discovered novel, potent CXCR4-selective antagonists binding within the orthosteric pocket with nanomolar affinity. The most active peptides effectively inhibited receptor signaling, suppressed chemokine-driven cell migration, and blocked CXCR4-driven HIV entry. Our results show that even the structurally minimal class A GPCRs are viable targets for de novo cyclic peptide discovery, highlighting the potential for uncovering ligands towards other members of the GPCR superfamily.

title: Perfluoroalkyl Anion Strategy to Construct Anion–π+ Type NIR-II Phototheranostic Agents for Enhanced Tumor Immunotherapy via Necroptosis/Ferroptosis
abstract: Anion-π+ photosensitizers (PSs) possess exceptional reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise organelle targeting that could disrupt intracellular metabolic homeostasis and induce nonapoptotic cell death, offering unique advantages in overcoming immunosuppression. However, previous reports mainly focused on modifying the π+ core but often overlooked the crucial role of anions. Herein, we present a facile perfluoroalkyl anion strategy to modulate the fluorescence intensity and ROS generation capacity of anion-π+ PSs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Strain turns carbon dioxide into circular polyesters
abstract: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.

title: DeepHartree: A Poisson-Coupled Neural Field for One-Shot Density Functional Theory
abstract: Linear-combination-of-atomic-orbital (LCAO) density functional theory (DFT) incurs steep costs when it constructs Coulomb terms and iterates the self-consistent field (SCF) equations. Matrix-learning approaches can bypass parts of this workflow, but their outputs inherit the dimensions and conventions of a fixed orbital basis. We introduce DeepHartree, a Poisson-coupled neural field that connects continuous real-space prediction to LCAO electronic structure. An E(3)-equivariant network predicts the Hartree potential, and the Poisson equation converts this potential into electron density.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Gold-Catalyzed Chemoselective Dearomative Ring-Opening Modes of Indoles
abstract: A gold-catalyzed dearomative cyclization of indoles with ynone-nitriles assisted by a Lewis or a Brønsted acid has been developed, which provides an efficient route to 4-azafluorenones via an unexpected indole ring-opening process. The key strategy involves the attack of an iminyl intermediate to the indoleninium species at its highly electrophilic C2 position, with both intermediates being generated spontaneously during the dearomatization process. By varying the gold catalyst and acid additives, the 1+1 and 2+1 component reactions can be achieved selectively.
