title: Subcrystal-Mediated Hetero-Crystallization Enables Phase-Controlled Zeolite Intergrowths with Multidimensional Disorder
abstract: Phase-controlled synthesis and comprehensive structural understanding of intergrowth zeolites remain challenging because of kinetic competition during crystallization and oversimplified structural models. Differences in nucleation kinetics between competing frameworks and framework interconversion during crystallization can decouple the initial synthesis composition from the final phase composition, while conventional stacking models cannot fully describe their structural complexity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Predicting Ternary Complex Stability through Binding Free-Energy Calculations in the Geometric Route
abstract: Molecular glue-induced targeted protein degradation is a powerful emerging therapeutic modality that exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation pathway to break down proteins associated with disease proliferation. At the structural level, degradation proceeds through the formation of a ternary complex induced by small molecules between the target protein and an E3 ligase. Unlike PROTACs, molecular glues do not require a chemical linker and tend to stabilize preexisting native protein–protein interactions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Local Electric Fields at Organic-Inorganic Hybrid Interfaces Drive Electrocatalysis
abstract: The local electric field generated at organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can profoundly influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet how molecular interfaces regulate local field distributions and reaction pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we combine grand-canonical density functional theory with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy to investigate CO2 reduction at cobalt phthalocyanine-copper (CoPc-Cu) interfaces. Density functional theory calculations show that CoPc creates a confined interfacial microenvironment and modifies the charge distribution at the Cu surface, producing non-uniform local electric fields that are experimentally probed using the vibrational Stark effect of adsorbed CO. Theory and experiment reveal that this field heterogeneity modifies CO adsorption across neighboring Cu sites and increases the adsorption-energy difference between adjacent CO intermediates, thereby lowering the barrier for C–C coupling. Consistent with this mechanism, CoPc-Cu exhibits an enhanced C2+/C1 product ratio, particularly at modest cathodic potentials where the confined hybrid interface is preserved. This work provides direct in situ evidence that organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can regulate electrocatalytic selectivity through local electric-field engineering, offering design principles for field-enhanced CO2 electroreduction.

title: Deep Learning-Based Non-Destructive Seafood Freshness Assessment: A Systematic Review of Sensing Technologies, Validation, and Deployment Readiness
abstract: Seafood freshness assessment is essential for quality control, shelf-life management, and supply-chain decisions, yet conventional sensory, chemical, and microbiological measurements are often destructive or laboratory-dependent. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on deep learning (DL)-based non-destructive seafood freshness assessment, focusing on sensing modality, model architecture, predictive performance, reference-standard validity, methodological robustness, and deployment readiness. Scopus and Web of Science records published in English from 2021 to 2026 were screened.

title: Engineering cyanobacterial carbonic anhydrase surface mutations for fast CO2 hydration and capture
abstract: Equilibration between CO 2 and the other forms of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is slow under ambient conditions, bottlenecked by the hydration of dissolved CO 2 to form bicarbonate and a proton. This step is often rate-limiting for aqueous CO 2 capture processes under ambient temperature and pressure, and is precisely the chemistry catalyzed by the family of carbonic anhydrase enzymes.
